You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

**[Section 7.12 --- Transition Services Agreement]{.underline}**

**Section 7.12(a) --- Obligation to Enter into TSA**

At or prior to the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall negotiate in good faith and enter into a Transition Services Agreement, on commercially reasonable terms and conditions, pursuant to which Seller shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Buyer (or its applicable Affiliates) the Transition Services described in Exhibit H hereto for a transition period following the Closing Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"). The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.

The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.

The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.

**Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**

All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.

The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.

In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.

Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.

**Section 7.12(c) --- Termination of Individual Services**

Buyer or Seller may terminate any individual Transition Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other party, specifying the Transition Service to be terminated and the effective date of such termination. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.1 of this Agreement.

Upon termination of any individual Transition Service, Buyer\'s obligation to pay TSA Fees with respect to such terminated Transition Service shall cease as of the effective date of termination, subject to Buyer\'s obligation to pay all TSA Fees accrued through such effective date and to reimburse Seller for any non-cancelable costs or commitments that Seller incurred prior to receipt of the termination notice in reasonable reliance on the continuation of such Transition Service, provided that Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such non-cancelable costs.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Transition Services Agreement provides for a notice period different from the ninety (90) day period specified in this Section 7.12(c), the notice period set forth in this Agreement shall control. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Section 7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to the termination of individual Transition Services, and any provision in the Transition Services Agreement purporting to require a longer or shorter notice period shall be of no force or effect.

**Section 7.12(d) --- Limitation of Liability**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that the aggregate liability of the Service Provider (and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents) to the Service Recipient under or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient to the Service Provider during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient (the \"**TSA Liability Cap**\").

For purposes of calculating the TSA Liability Cap during the first twelve (12) months of the Transition Period, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated based on the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient from the Closing Date through the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient. Thereafter, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated on a rolling twelve (12) month basis, measured from the date of assertion of the applicable claim and looking back twelve (12) months from such date.

The limitation set forth in this Section 7.12(d) shall not apply to:

> \(i\) claims arising from a party\'s fraud or willful misconduct;
>
> \(ii\) a party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations under the Transition Services Agreement; or
>
> \(iii\) a party\'s indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims arising out of the provision or receipt of Transition Services, to the extent such third-party claims result from the indemnifying party\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.

In no event shall either party be liable to the other party for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory, and regardless of whether such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages; provided, however, that this sentence shall not limit the liability of a party with respect to third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under the Transition Services Agreement.

The parties acknowledge and agree that the foregoing limitations on liability reflect the parties\' agreement regarding the allocation of risk under the Transition Services Agreement, and that neither party would have entered into this Agreement without such limitations.

**Section 7.12(e) --- Cooperation**

During the Transition Period, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own capability to perform the Transition Services independently and to reduce its reliance on Seller for the provision of such Transition Services as promptly as reasonably practicable. Buyer shall dedicate appropriate internal resources, including qualified personnel and financial resources, to the transition effort and shall develop and implement a transition plan in consultation with Seller.

Seller shall cooperate in good faith with Buyer\'s efforts to transition the Transition Services to Buyer\'s own systems, personnel, and third-party providers. Such cooperation shall include reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation of processes and procedures, and making Seller\'s personnel reasonably available for consultations during normal business hours.

Nothing in this Section 7.12 or the Transition Services Agreement shall require Seller to:

> \(i\) maintain any employee in employment or any contractor engagement solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services;
>
> \(ii\) acquire, license, or maintain any hardware, software, or other technology solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services, except to the extent that Seller was licensing or maintaining such technology for the benefit of the Business as of the Closing Date and the cost of such license or maintenance is included in the Fully-Loaded Cost;
>
> \(iii\) provide any Transition Service in a manner that would require Seller to violate any applicable Law or breach any contractual obligation to a third party; or
>
> \(iv\) disclose any trade secrets, proprietary information, or confidential business information of Seller that does not relate to the Business.

**Section 7.12(f) --- Service Standard; No Prioritization**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that Seller shall provide the Transition Services in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. The parties acknowledge that Seller\'s historical practices, methodologies, systems, and resource levels as applied to the Business during such twelve (12) month period shall serve as the benchmark for the required level of service under the Transition Services Agreement.

Nothing in the Transition Services Agreement shall obligate Seller to provide Transition Services at a level of quality, timeliness, or responsiveness that exceeds the level provided to the Business during such twelve (12) month period, or to prioritize the provision of Transition Services over services that Seller provides for its own account, for its retained business divisions, or for its other business units. Seller shall not be required to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices in connection with the provision of Transition Services that were not in use with respect to the Business during such twelve (12) month period.

The parties acknowledge and agree that Seller is not a professional services provider and that the Transition Services are being provided on an accommodation basis to facilitate the orderly transition of the Business to Buyer. Accordingly, the parties agree that the standard of care applicable to the provision of Transition Services shall be measured solely by reference to Seller\'s historical performance with respect to the Business and shall not be measured against any external industry standard, best-practice benchmark, or professional services standard.

**Section 7.12(g) --- Cross-Border Services**

To the extent that any Transition Services are provided in connection with the operations of the Monterrey Facility or involve the processing of personal data of employees located in Mexico, the Transition Services Agreement shall include commercially reasonable provisions to ensure compliance with applicable Mexican Law, including:

\"**Losses**\" means any and all damages, losses, liabilities, claims, demands, judgments, settlements, fines, penalties, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented attorneys\' fees, court costs, expert witness fees, and expenses of investigation and litigation), whether or not involving a third-party claim.
\"**Party**\" and \"**Parties**\" have the meanings set forth in the preamble.
\"**Person**\" means any individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, joint venture, association, trust, unincorporated organization, Governmental Authority, or other entity.
\"**Renewal Term**\" means each successive six (6)-month period following the Initial Term, as further described in Section 5.2.
\"**Representatives**\" means, with respect to any Person, such Person\'s directors, officers, employees, agents, consultants, advisors, accountants, attorneys, and other representatives.
\"**SAP System**\" has the meaning set forth in the definition of \"ERP System.\"
\"**Service Charges**\" has the meaning set forth in the definition of \"Fees.\"
\"**Service Manager**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.2.
\"**Service Provider**\" has the meaning set forth in the preamble.

\"**Service Provider Materials**\" means any and all tools, methodologies, templates, processes, frameworks, software (including source code and object code), algorithms, models, know-how, techniques, inventions, discoveries, works of authorship, or other intellectual property owned by or licensed to Service Provider (or any of its Affiliates), whether existing prior to the Effective Date or developed or created during the Term, that are used, developed, or utilized by Service Provider in connection with the performance of the Services under this Agreement.
\"**Service Recipient**\" has the meaning set forth in the preamble.
\"**Service Recipient Materials**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 7.2.
\"**Service Standard**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 3.1.
\"**Services**\" means the transition services described in Schedules A through F attached hereto, as such Schedules may be amended from time to time in accordance with this Agreement.
\"**Steering Committee**\" has the meaning set forth in Section 4.1.

\"**Tax**\" or \"**Taxes**\" means all federal, state, local, and foreign income, gross receipts, license, payroll, employment, excise, severance, stamp, occupation, premium, windfall profits, customs duties, capital stock, franchise, profits, withholding, social security (or similar), unemployment, disability, real property, personal property, sales, use, transfer, registration, value-added, alternative or add-on minimum, estimated, and other taxes of any kind, together with any interest, penalty, or addition thereto, whether disputed or not.
\"**Term**\" means the Initial Term plus any Renewal Terms, as further described in Article 5.
\"**Transaction Documents**\" has the meaning ascribed to such term in the APA.

\"**Transferred Employees**\" means those approximately one thousand one hundred eighty (1,180) employees of the Business who will transfer to Trident at the Closing in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Purchase Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 2 --- SERVICES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1** *Provision of Services.* Commencing on the Effective Date and continuing during the Term, Service Provider shall provide, or shall cause its Affiliates or designees to provide, to Service Recipient the Services described in the following Schedules:
> \(a\) **Schedule A** --- Financial Reporting & Accounting Services;
> \(b\) **Schedule B** --- Information Technology Services;
> \(c\) **Schedule C** --- Human Resources Services;
> \(d\) **Schedule D** --- Supply Chain & Procurement Services;
> \(e\) **Schedule E** --- Regulatory & EHS Compliance Services; and
> \(f\) **Schedule F** --- Treasury & Tax Services.

The six (6) service categories set forth above correspond to the service categories identified in Exhibit H to the Purchase Agreement. The Services will be provided by an aggregate of approximately one hundred (100) full-time equivalent Service Provider personnel allocated across the service categories as follows: twenty-two (22) FTEs for Financial Reporting & Accounting; thirty-one (31) FTEs for Information Technology; eighteen (18) FTEs for Human Resources; fourteen (14) FTEs for Supply Chain & Procurement; eight (8) FTEs for Regulatory & EHS Compliance; and seven (7) FTEs for Treasury & Tax. The specific scope, deliverables, personnel, systems, and migration milestones for each Service category are set forth in the applicable Schedule. In the event of any conflict between the terms of an individual Schedule and the terms of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Schedule expressly and specifically provides otherwise.

**Section 2.2** *Scope Limitations.* The Services to be provided by Service Provider under this Agreement are limited solely and exclusively to those services expressly described in Schedules A through F. Service Provider shall not be obligated to provide any service or perform any function that is not expressly described in the applicable Schedule. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Service Provider shall not be obligated to: (a) hire additional employees or engage additional contractors solely for the purpose of providing the Services; (b) acquire, lease, or license additional equipment, software, or other assets solely for the purpose of providing the Services; (c) maintain any third-party software license, service contract, or other agreement beyond its current term or renewal period solely for the purpose of providing the Services; or (d) make any capital expenditure solely for the purpose of providing the Services. The scope of each Service is as described in the applicable Schedule as of the Effective Date, and no expansion, modification, or enhancement of any Service shall be required of Service Provider except as may be mutually agreed in writing by the Parties.

**Section 2.3** *Exclusive Remedy.* Service Recipient\'s sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by Service Provider to perform any of the Services in accordance with this Agreement shall be as expressly set forth in Article 9 (Indemnification) and Article 10 (Limitation of Liability). Service Recipient shall have no other right or remedy at law or in equity with respect to any such failure, except as expressly set forth herein.

**Section 2.4** *Subcontracting.* Service Provider may, in its sole discretion, subcontract or delegate any or all of the Services to qualified third-party subcontractors or to Affiliates of Service Provider; provided that Service Provider shall remain fully responsible for the performance of any subcontracted or delegated Services and for the acts and omissions of any such subcontractor or Affiliate to the same extent as if Service Provider had performed such Services directly. Service Provider shall ensure that any subcontractor or Affiliate performing Services is bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in Article 8.
**[ARTICLE 3 --- SERVICE STANDARDS]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1** *Standard of Performance.* Service Provider shall perform, or cause to be performed, each of the Services at a level of quality, timeliness, and competence at least equal to or better than the level at which such services were provided to the Business during the twenty-four (24) month period prior to the Closing Date, and in all cases in accordance with industry best practices applicable to each such Service (the \"**Service Standard**\"). Service Provider shall allocate sufficient resources, including qualified personnel and appropriate systems, to meet the Service Standard at all times during the Term. In the event of any dispute regarding the Service Standard, the Parties shall refer the matter to the Steering Committee for resolution in accordance with Article 4.

**Section 3.2** *No Guarantee of Results.* Notwithstanding Section 3.1 or any other provision of this Agreement, Service Provider does not guarantee any particular outcome, result, or deliverable from the provision of the Services. Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to performing the Services in accordance with the Service Standard, and Service Provider shall not be liable for any failure to achieve a particular business outcome or result so long as the Services are performed in accordance with the Service Standard.

**Section 3.3** *Cooperation.* Service Recipient shall cooperate with Service Provider and shall provide, in a timely manner, all information, data, access, approvals, decisions, and assistance reasonably necessary for Service Provider to perform the Services in accordance with this Agreement. Service Recipient acknowledges and agrees that Service Provider\'s ability to meet the Service Standard may be materially and adversely affected by Service Recipient\'s failure to cooperate or to provide timely information, access, or decisions as contemplated by this Section 3.3. Service Provider shall not be liable for any failure or delay in performing the Services to the extent such failure or delay is attributable to Service Recipient\'s failure to comply with this Section 3.3.

321: **[ARTICLE 4 --- GOVERNANCE]{.underline}**
322: 
323: **Section 4.1** *Steering Committee.* Within ten (10) Business Days of the Effective Date, each Party shall designate two (2) senior representatives to serve on a joint transition steering committee (the \"**Steering Committee**\"). The initial designees of the Steering Committee shall be as follows:
324: 
325: > \(a\) **For Service Provider (Polaris):**
326: >
327: > \(i\) David K. Okafor, Chief Financial Officer; and
328: >
329: > \(ii\) Sharon M. Petrosian, General Counsel.
330: >
331: > \(b\) **For Service Recipient (Trident):**
332: >
333: > \(i\) Patricia N. Suresh, Chief Financial Officer; and
334: >
335: > \(ii\) Robert F. Collier, General Counsel.
336: 
337: Either Party may replace its designees on the Steering Committee at any time upon written notice to the other Party; provided that any replacement designee shall be a senior officer of the designating Party with sufficient authority to make decisions on behalf of such Party with respect to matters arising under this Agreement. The Steering Committee shall meet at least once per calendar month (or more frequently as mutually agreed or as circumstances require) to review and discuss the status of service delivery, migration milestones, key performance metrics, open issues, and any disputes or concerns raised by either Party. Meetings may be held in person or by video or telephone conference. Each Party shall bear its own costs associated with participation in the Steering Committee. The Steering Committee shall not have the authority to amend, modify, or waive any provision of this Agreement, which may be done only in accordance with Section 15.6.
338: 
339: **Section 4.2** *Service Managers.* In addition to its Steering Committee designees, each Party shall designate a Service Manager for each Service category (each, a \"**Service Manager**\") who shall serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day operational matters relating to such Service category. Each Service Manager shall be an individual with relevant operational expertise and sufficient authority to manage day-to-day decisions within the scope of the applicable Service category. Service Managers shall report regularly to the Steering Committee and shall escalate to the Steering Committee any issues that cannot be resolved at the operational level within a reasonable period of time. Each Party shall notify the other Party in writing of the identity and contact information of its Service Managers within five (5) Business Days of the Effective Date.
340: 
341: **Section 4.3** *Key Personnel.* Service Provider shall ensure that the individuals identified on Schedule H attached hereto (the \"**Key Personnel**\") are assigned to perform the Services during the Term at the FTE allocation levels set forth on Schedule H. Service Provider shall not reassign, transfer, terminate (other than for cause as determined by Service Provider in its reasonable judgment), or otherwise remove any Key Personnel from the performance of the Services without the prior written consent of Service Recipient, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. In the event that any Key Personnel individual voluntarily resigns, becomes permanently disabled, or is terminated for cause, Service Provider shall promptly notify Service Recipient and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to replace such individual with a person of substantially similar qualifications, experience, and skill within thirty (30) days, subject to Service Recipient\'s prior written approval of the replacement (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). Service Provider acknowledges that the Key Personnel possess specialized knowledge of the Business and that their continued involvement is material to the successful transition of the Business to Service Recipient.
342: 
343: **Section 4.4** *Reporting.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient, within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, a written report summarizing the Services performed during such month (each, a \"**Monthly Report**\"). Each Monthly Report shall include, at a minimum: (a) hours worked by each FTE assigned to the Services, broken down by Service category; (b) a summary of any material issues, disruptions, or failures in service delivery; (c) a status update on migration milestones, including any variances from the milestone schedule set forth in the applicable Schedule; and (d) such other information as the Steering Committee may reasonably request from time to time.
344: 
345: **[ARTICLE 5 --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**
346: 
347: **Section 5.1** *Initial Term.* This Agreement shall become effective on the Closing Date and shall continue for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Initial Term**\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 5. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement shall have no force or effect unless and until the Closing occurs under the Purchase Agreement.
348: 
349: **Section 5.2** *Automatic Renewal.* Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods (each, a \"**Renewal Term**\"), unless Service Provider delivers written notice of non-renewal to Service Recipient at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. The Agreement may be renewed for up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms pursuant to this Section 5.2. During any Renewal Term, all terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, including the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule, subject to any adjustments expressly provided for herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the burden of providing notice of non-renewal rests solely with Service Provider; failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice of non-renewal shall result in automatic renewal for the next succeeding Renewal Term (subject to the two (2) Renewal Term maximum).
350: 
351: **Section 5.3** *Termination of Individual Services.* Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice specifies in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date of termination. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect the continuance of any other Service being provided under this Agreement. Upon termination of any individual Service, the corresponding Fees for such Service shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of such termination.
352: 
353: **Section 5.4** *Termination for Cause.* Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice to the other Party if the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the breach is of such a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be deemed in default so long as it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion; provided, however, that no cure period shall extend beyond ninety (90) days from the date of the initial notice of breach.
354: 
355: **Section 5.5** *Effect of Termination.* Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part):
356: 
357: > \(a\) Service Provider\'s obligation to provide the terminated or expired Services shall immediately cease as of the effective date of such termination or expiration;
358: >
359: > \(b\) Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider all accrued but unpaid Fees and expenses for Services actually performed through the effective date of termination or expiration, which payment shall be made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration;
360: >
361: > \(c\) each Party shall promptly return to the other Party, or at the other Party\'s election destroy and certify in writing the destruction of, all Confidential Information of the other Party that relates to the terminated or expired Services, except to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Law or bona fide document retention policies (in which case such retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of Article 8); and
362: >
363: > \(d\) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services shall cease, except as expressly provided in Section 5.6 (Survival).
364: 
365: **Section 5.6** *Survival.* The provisions of Article 1 (Definitions), Article 7 (Intellectual Property), Article 8 (Confidentiality), Article 9 (Indemnification), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Representations and Warranties), Article 13 (Insurance), Article 14 (Audit Rights), and Article 15 (General Provisions) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement in accordance with their respective terms.
366: 
367: **[ARTICLE 6 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**
368: 
369: **Section 6.1** *Service Charges.* In consideration for the provision of the Services, Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule (Schedule G) for each Service during the Term. The Fees for each Service category are calculated on a cost-plus basis reflecting Service Provider\'s fully-loaded cost of providing the applicable Service (including personnel costs, allocated overhead, and systems costs), plus a markup as set forth on the Fee Schedule. The Fees represent the sole compensation to which Service Provider is entitled for the provision of the Services, and Service Provider shall not charge Service Recipient for any internal costs, overhead, or administrative expenses except as expressly reflected in the Fee Schedule.
370: 
371: **Section 6.2** *Invoicing.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient a monthly invoice within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, setting forth in reasonable detail the Services performed during such month, the applicable FTE hours, and the Fees due for such month. Each invoice shall be accompanied by such supporting documentation as Service Recipient may reasonably request to verify the accuracy of the amounts invoiced. Invoices shall be delivered to the attention of Service Recipient\'s Service Manager for the applicable Service category, with a copy to Service Recipient\'s Chief Financial Officer.
372: 
373: **Section 6.3** *Payment.* Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within a commercially reasonable time following receipt thereof. All payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Service Provider in writing from time to time.
374: 
375: **Section 6.4** *Fee Escalation.* The Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule are fixed for the duration of the Term and shall not be subject to escalation or adjustment, except as expressly provided in this Agreement.
376: 
377: **Section 6.5** *Taxes.* All Fees stated in this Agreement and on the Fee Schedule are exclusive of any applicable sales, use, value-added, goods and services, or similar Taxes (collectively, \"**Transaction Taxes**\"). Service Recipient shall be responsible for and shall pay, or reimburse Service Provider for, all Transaction Taxes imposed on or with respect to the Services, other than Taxes measured by Service Provider\'s net income, capital, or franchise. Service Provider shall separately state any Transaction Taxes on its invoices. Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize Transaction Taxes and shall cooperate in good faith with the other Party to obtain any available exemptions or reduced rates for such Taxes.
378: 
379: **Section 6.6** *Disputed Amounts.* If Service Recipient disputes any amount set forth on an invoice in good faith, Service Recipient shall: (a) pay the undisputed portion of such invoice when due in accordance with Section 6.3; (b) provide written notice to Service Provider of the disputed amount, specifying in reasonable detail the basis for the dispute, within fifteen (15) Business Days after receipt of the applicable invoice; and (c) work in good faith with Service Provider to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days after such notice. If the Parties are unable to resolve the dispute within such thirty (30)-day period, either Party may escalate the matter to the Steering Committee. Pending resolution of any disputed amount, Service Provider shall continue to perform the Services without interruption.
380: 
381: **[ARTICLE 7 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**
382: 
383: **Section 7.1** *Service Provider Materials --- License Grant.* Service Provider hereby grants to Service Recipient a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, and create derivative works of any Service Provider Materials (including any tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, or know-how) developed or utilized by Service Provider in connection with the performance of the Services under this Agreement. This license shall include the right to sublicense to Service Recipient\'s Affiliates, successors, and assigns, and shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason. For the avoidance of doubt, the foregoing license extends to all Service Provider Materials that are used, in whole or in part, in the delivery of any of the Services, regardless of whether such Service Provider Materials were created specifically for the Services or existed prior to the Effective Date and were adapted or applied in the course of service delivery. Nothing in this Section 7.1 shall be construed to transfer ownership of any Service Provider Materials to Service Recipient; Service Provider retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Service Provider Materials, subject to the license granted herein.
384: 
385: **Section 7.2** *Service Recipient Materials.* Service Recipient retains all right, title, and interest in and to any data, materials, information, documents, or other content provided by Service Recipient to Service Provider for purposes of the Services (collectively, \"**Service Recipient Materials**\"). Service Provider shall use the Service Recipient Materials solely for the purpose of performing the Services under this Agreement and for no other purpose. Upon termination or expiration of any Service or this Agreement, Service Provider shall promptly return or, at Service Recipient\'s election, destroy all Service Recipient Materials in its possession or control.
386: 
387: **Section 7.3** *Feedback.* To the extent that Service Recipient provides any suggestions, ideas, enhancement requests, recommendations, or other feedback to Service Provider regarding the Service Provider Materials or any other intellectual property of Service Provider (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Service Recipient hereby assigns to Service Provider all right, title, and interest in and to such Feedback and agrees that Service Provider is free to use, disclose, reproduce, license, and otherwise distribute and exploit such Feedback as it sees fit, without obligation or restriction of any kind. Service Recipient acknowledges that this assignment is irrevocable and that no additional consideration is required.
388: 
389: **[ARTICLE 8 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
390: 
391: **Section 8.1** *Confidentiality Obligations.* Each Party agrees to hold the other Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence and to protect such Confidential Information using the same degree of care that it uses to protect its own confidential information of like kind, but in no event less than a reasonable degree of care. Neither Party shall disclose the other Party\'s Confidential Information to any Person, except to its Representatives who have a bona fide need to know such information for the purpose of performing obligations or exercising rights under this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 8. Each Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 8 by its Representatives. Neither Party shall use the other Party\'s Confidential Information for any purpose other than in connection with the performance of its obligations or the exercise of its rights under this Agreement. Without limiting the foregoing, neither Party shall reverse engineer, decompile, or disassemble any Confidential Information of the other Party.
392: 
393: **Section 8.2** *Exceptions.* The obligations set forth in Section 8.1 shall not apply to any information that:
394: 
395: > \(a\) is or becomes publicly available other than as a result of a disclosure by the Receiving Party or its Representatives in breach of this Agreement;
396: >
397: > \(b\) was already known to the Receiving Party at the time of disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party;
398: >
399: > \(c\) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by competent written records of the Receiving Party; or
400: >
401: > \(d\) is received by the Receiving Party from a third party who is not, to the Receiving Party\'s knowledge, bound by any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.
402: 
403: In addition, the Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by Applicable Law, regulation, or order of a Governmental Authority, or by the rules and regulations of a stock exchange on which the Receiving Party\'s (or its parent\'s) securities are listed; provided that the Receiving Party shall, to the extent legally permissible, provide prompt written notice to the Disclosing Party of such required disclosure so as to enable the Disclosing Party to seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy. If a protective order or other remedy is not obtained, the Receiving Party shall disclose only that portion of the Confidential Information that it is legally required to disclose and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain reliable assurance that confidential treatment will be given to such disclosed information.
404: 
405: **Section 8.3** *Survival of Confidentiality.* The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 8 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years following the effective date of such expiration or termination.
406: 
407: **Section 8.4** *Data Privacy.* Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws of the United States in connection with its performance under this Agreement, including with respect to the collection, use, processing, storage, transfer, and disposal of any personally identifiable information of employees, customers, or other individuals. Each Party shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.
408: 
409: **[ARTICLE 9 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
410: 
411: **Section 9.1** *Service Recipient Indemnification.* Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"**Service Provider Indemnitee**\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Provider Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:
412: 
413: > \(a\) Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance on the Services or the results thereof;
414: >
415: > \(b\) any breach by Service Recipient of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation under this Agreement;
416: >
417: > \(c\) any negligent or wrongful act or omission of Service Recipient or its employees, agents, or contractors in connection with this Agreement; or
418: >
419: > \(d\) any claim by a third party arising out of Service Recipient\'s use of the Services or any deliverables provided hereunder, except to the extent such claim arises from Service Provider\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
420: 
421: **Section 9.2** *Service Provider Indemnification.* Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"**Service Recipient Indemnitee**\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Recipient Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:
422: 
423: > \(a\) any gross negligence or willful misconduct of Service Provider, its Affiliates, or their respective employees, agents, or contractors in performing the Services;
424: >
425: > \(b\) any breach by Service Provider of any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation under this Agreement; or
426: >
427: > \(c\) any violation of Applicable Law by Service Provider, its Affiliates, or their respective employees, agents, or contractors in performing the Services.
428: 
429: **Section 9.3** *Indemnification Procedures.* The following procedures shall apply to any claim for indemnification under this Article 9:
430: 
431: > \(a\) **Notice.** The Party seeking indemnification (the \"**Indemnified Party**\") shall promptly notify the other Party (the \"**Indemnifying Party**\") in writing of any claim, demand, suit, action, or proceeding for which indemnification is sought (a \"**Claim**\"), specifying in reasonable detail the nature of the Claim and the amount of Losses incurred or expected to be incurred (to the extent then known). The failure by the Indemnified Party to give timely notice shall not relieve the Indemnifying Party of its indemnification obligations except to the extent that the Indemnifying Party is actually and materially prejudiced by such failure.
432: >
433: > \(b\) **Defense of Third-Party Claims.** Upon receipt of notice of a Claim involving a third-party claim, the Indemnifying Party shall have the right, but not the obligation, to assume the defense of such third-party claim, including the employment of counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Party, at the Indemnifying Party\'s sole cost and expense. If the Indemnifying Party assumes the defense, the Indemnified Party may participate in the defense at its own expense, but the Indemnifying Party shall control all aspects of the defense and any related settlement or compromise. If the Indemnifying Party does not assume the defense within thirty (30) days after receipt of notice, the Indemnified Party may defend the third-party claim at the Indemnifying Party\'s expense.
434: >
435: > \(c\) **Settlement.** The Indemnifying Party shall not consent to entry of any judgment or enter into any settlement or compromise with respect to a third-party claim without the prior written consent of the Indemnified Party (such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), unless such judgment, settlement, or compromise: (i) includes an unconditional release of the Indemnified Party from all liability with respect to such claim; (ii) does not impose any non-monetary obligations on the Indemnified Party; and (iii) does not contain any admission of liability or wrongdoing by the Indemnified Party.
436: >
437: > \(d\) **Cooperation.** The Indemnified Party shall cooperate in all reasonable respects with the Indemnifying Party and its counsel in the defense of any third-party claim, including by making available relevant records, information, and personnel.
438: 
439: **[ARTICLE 10 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**
440: 
441: **Section 10.1** *Aggregate Liability Cap.* Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Service Provider\'s aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or any other legal or equitable theory, shall not exceed an amount equal to two hundred percent (200%) of the total Service Charges actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider under this Agreement as of the date of the applicable claim (the \"**Liability Cap**\"). For the avoidance of doubt, the Liability Cap shall apply to all claims in the aggregate and not on a per-claim basis. This Section 10.1 shall not limit Service Provider\'s liability for fraud, willful misconduct, or breaches of Article 8 (Confidentiality).
442: 
443: **Section 10.2** *Consequential Damages.* SERVICE PROVIDER HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS AGAINST SERVICE RECIPIENT FOR CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, DIMINUTION OF VALUE, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SUCH DAMAGES ARE BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, AND REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SERVICE PROVIDER HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING WAIVER SHALL APPLY EVEN IN THE EVENT OF THE FAILURE OF ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF ANY REMEDY.
444: 
445: **Section 10.3** *Essential Basis.* The Parties acknowledge and agree that the limitations and exclusions of liability set forth in this Article 10 represent a fundamental element of the basis of the bargain between the Parties and that the Parties would not have entered into this Agreement absent such limitations and exclusions. Such limitations and exclusions shall apply regardless of the failure of essential purpose of any remedy provided herein and shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement.
446: 
447: **[ARTICLE 11 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
448: 
449: **Section 11.1** *Mutual Representations.* Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party as of the Effective Date that:
450: 
451: > \(a\) it is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its incorporation;
452: >
453: > \(b\) it has the full corporate power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby;
454: >

**Section 4.1** *Steering Committee.* Within ten (10) Business Days of the Effective Date, each Party shall designate two (2) senior representatives to serve on a joint transition steering committee (the \"**Steering Committee**\"). The initial designees of the Steering Committee shall be as follows:
> \(a\) **For Service Provider (Polaris):**
> \(i\) David K. Okafor, Chief Financial Officer; and
> \(ii\) Sharon M. Petrosian, General Counsel.
> \(b\) **For Service Recipient (Trident):**
> \(i\) Patricia N. Suresh, Chief Financial Officer; and
> \(ii\) Robert F. Collier, General Counsel.

Either Party may replace its designees on the Steering Committee at any time upon written notice to the other Party; provided that any replacement designee shall be a senior officer of the designating Party with sufficient authority to make decisions on behalf of such Party with respect to matters arising under this Agreement. The Steering Committee shall meet at least once per calendar month (or more frequently as mutually agreed or as circumstances require) to review and discuss the status of service delivery, migration milestones, key performance metrics, open issues, and any disputes or concerns raised by either Party. Meetings may be held in person or by video or telephone conference. Each Party shall bear its own costs associated with participation in the Steering Committee. The Steering Committee shall not have the authority to amend, modify, or waive any provision of this Agreement, which may be done only in accordance with Section 15.6.

**Section 4.2** *Service Managers.* In addition to its Steering Committee designees, each Party shall designate a Service Manager for each Service category (each, a \"**Service Manager**\") who shall serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day operational matters relating to such Service category. Each Service Manager shall be an individual with relevant operational expertise and sufficient authority to manage day-to-day decisions within the scope of the applicable Service category. Service Managers shall report regularly to the Steering Committee and shall escalate to the Steering Committee any issues that cannot be resolved at the operational level within a reasonable period of time. Each Party shall notify the other Party in writing of the identity and contact information of its Service Managers within five (5) Business Days of the Effective Date.

**Section 4.3** *Key Personnel.* Service Provider shall ensure that the individuals identified on Schedule H attached hereto (the \"**Key Personnel**\") are assigned to perform the Services during the Term at the FTE allocation levels set forth on Schedule H. Service Provider shall not reassign, transfer, terminate (other than for cause as determined by Service Provider in its reasonable judgment), or otherwise remove any Key Personnel from the performance of the Services without the prior written consent of Service Recipient, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. In the event that any Key Personnel individual voluntarily resigns, becomes permanently disabled, or is terminated for cause, Service Provider shall promptly notify Service Recipient and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to replace such individual with a person of substantially similar qualifications, experience, and skill within thirty (30) days, subject to Service Recipient\'s prior written approval of the replacement (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). Service Provider acknowledges that the Key Personnel possess specialized knowledge of the Business and that their continued involvement is material to the successful transition of the Business to Service Recipient.

**Section 4.4** *Reporting.* Service Provider shall deliver to Service Recipient, within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month, a written report summarizing the Services performed during such month (each, a \"**Monthly Report**\"). Each Monthly Report shall include, at a minimum: (a) hours worked by each FTE assigned to the Services, broken down by Service category; (b) a summary of any material issues, disruptions, or failures in service delivery; (c) a status update on migration milestones, including any variances from the milestone schedule set forth in the applicable Schedule; and (d) such other information as the Steering Committee may reasonably request from time to time.
**[ARTICLE 5 --- TERM AND TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1** *Initial Term.* This Agreement shall become effective on the Closing Date and shall continue for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Initial Term**\"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with this Article 5. For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement shall have no force or effect unless and until the Closing occurs under the Purchase Agreement.

**Section 5.2** *Automatic Renewal.* Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods (each, a \"**Renewal Term**\"), unless Service Provider delivers written notice of non-renewal to Service Recipient at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. The Agreement may be renewed for up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms pursuant to this Section 5.2. During any Renewal Term, all terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, including the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule, subject to any adjustments expressly provided for herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the burden of providing notice of non-renewal rests solely with Service Provider; failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice of non-renewal shall result in automatic renewal for the next succeeding Renewal Term (subject to the two (2) Renewal Term maximum).

**Section 5.3** *Termination of Individual Services.* Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice specifies in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date of termination. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect the continuance of any other Service being provided under this Agreement. Upon termination of any individual Service, the corresponding Fees for such Service shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of such termination.

**Section 5.4** *Termination for Cause.* Either Party may terminate this Agreement in whole, or with respect to any individual Service, upon written notice to the other Party if the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail. If the breach is of such a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be deemed in default so long as it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion; provided, however, that no cure period shall extend beyond ninety (90) days from the date of the initial notice of breach.
**Section 5.5** *Effect of Termination.* Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part):
> \(a\) Service Provider\'s obligation to provide the terminated or expired Services shall immediately cease as of the effective date of such termination or expiration;

> \(b\) Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider all accrued but unpaid Fees and expenses for Services actually performed through the effective date of termination or expiration, which payment shall be made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration;

> \(c\) each Party shall promptly return to the other Party, or at the other Party\'s election destroy and certify in writing the destruction of, all Confidential Information of the other Party that relates to the terminated or expired Services, except to the extent that retention is required by Applicable Law or bona fide document retention policies (in which case such retained Confidential Information shall remain subject to the confidentiality obligations of Article 8); and
> \(d\) all rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the terminated or expired Services shall cease, except as expressly provided in Section 5.6 (Survival).

**Section 5.6** *Survival.* The provisions of Article 1 (Definitions), Article 7 (Intellectual Property), Article 8 (Confidentiality), Article 9 (Indemnification), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Representations and Warranties), Article 13 (Insurance), Article 14 (Audit Rights), and Article 15 (General Provisions) shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement in accordance with their respective terms.
**[ARTICLE 6 --- FEES AND PAYMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1** *Service Charges.* In consideration for the provision of the Services, Service Recipient shall pay to Service Provider the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule (Schedule G) for each Service during the Term. The Fees for each Service category are calculated on a cost-plus basis reflecting Service Provider\'s fully-loaded cost of providing the applicable Service (including personnel costs, allocated overhead, and systems costs), plus a markup as set forth on the Fee Schedule. **SCHEDULE A** **FINANCIAL REPORTING & ACCOUNTING SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following financial reporting and accounting services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **General Ledger Maintenance.** Continued maintenance and operation of the Business\'s general ledger within Service Provider\'s SAP S/4HANA enterprise resource planning system, utilizing the legacy Specialty Coatings Division chart of accounts, account hierarchies, and cost center structures. This includes the posting of journal entries, maintenance of the chart of accounts, intercompany accounting entries, and sub-ledger reconciliation.

> \(b\) **Accounts Payable Processing.** Processing of vendor invoices, verification of purchase order matching (three-way match), coding and posting of approved invoices, execution of payment runs (check, ACH, and wire transfer), vendor statement reconciliation, and management of the AP aging schedule for the Business.

> \(c\) **Accounts Receivable Processing and Collections Support.** Customer invoice generation, posting of cash receipts, application of payments to open invoices, management of the AR aging schedule, credit memo processing, and support for past-due collections activities in coordination with Service Recipient\'s sales personnel.

> \(d\) **Monthly Financial Close Support.** Assistance with the monthly financial close process for the Business, including preparation and posting of standard and recurring journal entries (accruals, prepaid amortizations, depreciation), account reconciliations (bank, intercompany, balance sheet), intercompany eliminations, and resolution of reconciling items. Service Provider shall complete its portion of the monthly close process within eight (8) Business Days following the end of each calendar month.

> \(e\) **Management Reporting Package.** Preparation and delivery of a monthly management reporting package for the Business, consisting of: (i) income statement (P&L) by product line and facility; (ii) balance sheet; (iii) statement of cash flows; (iv) variance analysis comparing actual results to budget and prior year; and (v) such other reports as may be reasonably requested by the Steering Committee.

> \(c\) **Cybersecurity Monitoring and Incident Response.** Monitoring of the Business\'s IT environment for cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents using Service Provider\'s existing security information and event management (SIEM) platform, endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools, and intrusion detection systems. 25: **[Section 1: Purpose and Scope of Playbook]{.underline}**
26: 
27: Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. is a diversified industrial conglomerate incorporated in Delaware, with approximately \$3.2 billion in annual revenue across four operating divisions: Advanced Materials, Specialty Coatings, Precision Components, and Industrial Automation. Polaris is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and maintains domestic and international operations including a manufacturing facility in Monterrey, Mexico.
28: 
29: Divestitures of individual business units frequently require Polaris to provide post-closing transition services to buyers. This need arises because Polaris\'s shared-services infrastructure --- encompassing IT, HR/Payroll, Finance/Accounting, Supply Chain/Procurement, Regulatory/EHS, and Treasury/Tax functions --- supports multiple divisions simultaneously through common personnel and integrated systems. Approximately 100 full-time equivalents across these service categories typically support any single division alongside other Polaris businesses. These personnel remain Polaris employees after closing, necessitating a Transition Services Agreement under which Polaris continues to perform certain functions on behalf of the buyer for a defined transition period.
30: 
31: The purpose of this Playbook is to protect Polaris\'s interests as Service Provider by:
32: 
33: > • **(a)** Limiting liability exposure arising from the provision of transition services;
34: >
35: > • **(b)** Preserving Polaris\'s operational flexibility to manage its own workforce and systems;
36: >
37: > • **(c)** Protecting Polaris\'s proprietary intellectual property, systems, and know-how;
38: >
39: > • **(d)** Ensuring adequate compensation for the administrative burden and resource diversion inherent in service delivery; and
40: >
41: > • **(e)** Maintaining compliance with the terms and constraints set forth in the governing purchase agreement.
42: 
43: This Playbook should always be read in conjunction with the applicable Asset Purchase Agreement (or Stock Purchase Agreement, as applicable). Where the APA mandates specific TSA terms --- including service standard, term, fee cap, or liability structure --- the APA controls and those terms are not subject to further negotiation in the TSA. The Playbook serves as the benchmark against which any buyer\'s draft TSA is evaluated, and any deviation from the positions stated herein should be flagged, analyzed, and escalated as appropriate.

47: **[2.1 Standard of Performance]{.underline}**
48: 
49:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
50:                                       **Position**
51:   ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
52:   **Target**                          Services shall be provided *\"in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality provided to the Business during the twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date.\"* No obligation to exceed historical service levels. No obligation to prioritize Service Recipient over Polaris\'s own internal business needs.
53: 
54:   **Fallback**                        Add *\"using commercially reasonable efforts\"* after *\"substantially consistent\"* language. This is the maximum concession.
