57: **Key Negotiation Points:**
58: 
59: > • **Lookback Period:** The lookback period is twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date. Do not accept a 24-month or longer lookback period. A longer lookback may capture atypical service levels (e.g., pre-pandemic staffing, special project surges) that are not representative of current operations.
60: >
61: > • **\"Substantially Consistent\" Language:** The operative standard is *\"substantially consistent with,\"* which permits reasonable variation. Reject language such as *\"equal to or better than,\"* *\"at least equal to,\"* or *\"no less favorable than.\"* These formulations impose a floor that ratchets upward and does not permit any reduction or variation, however reasonable.
62: >
63: > • **Reject \"Best Practices\" and Similar Standards:** References to *\"industry best practices,\"* *\"commercially reasonable best efforts,\"* or other aspirational benchmarks must be rejected. These terms are undefined, subjective, invite disputes, and impose a standard that may materially exceed what Polaris historically provided to the divested business. Polaris is not a third-party service provider competing for business --- it is providing transitional support as an accommodation.
64: >
65: > • **Not a Guarantor:** Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to making available the same general type and level of resources as historically deployed. Service Provider does not guarantee specific outcomes, results, or service levels beyond what was historically provided.
66: >
67: > • **APA Precedence:** If the APA specifies a service standard (e.g., in the TSA covenant section or an exhibit), that APA standard controls and the TSA cannot impose a more stringent requirement.
68: 
69: **[2.2 Exclusions from Service Obligation]{.underline}**
70: 
71: Service Provider has no obligation to:
72: 
73: > • **(a)** Provide services not described in the applicable Service Schedules;
74: >
75: > • **(b)** Hire additional personnel or acquire additional resources beyond those in place as of the Closing Date;
76: >
77: > • **(c)** Provide services that would violate applicable law or regulation;
78: >
79: > • **(d)** Provide services that would breach any third-party agreement to which Polaris is a party (including software licenses, vendor contracts, or confidentiality agreements);
80: >
81: > • **(e)** Provide advice of any kind --- legal, tax, financial, or strategic.
82: 
83: Service Provider may modify the manner of delivering services to the extent such modifications are consistent with changes made to services provided to Polaris\'s own businesses (e.g., system upgrades, vendor changes, process improvements applied company-wide).
84: 
85: **[Section 3: Term and Termination]{.underline}**
86: 
87: **[3.1 Maximum Term]{.underline}**
88: 
89:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
90:                                       **Position**
91:   ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
92:   **Target**                          Fixed term not to exceed **18 months** from the Closing Date. Hard stop. No automatic renewal. Extensions require: (i) mutual written agreement, (ii) pricing at cost-plus-15%, (iii) maximum extension of 6 months (total possible term: 24 months only upon mutual agreement).
93: 
94:   **Fallback**                        Mutual written extension option at cost-plus-10% (minimum). Never accept automatic renewals.
95:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
96: 
97: **Key Negotiation Points:**
98: 
99: > • The 18-month maximum is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12 in standard Polaris deals. The TSA cannot exceed the APA-mandated term.
100: >
101: > • **Automatic renewal provisions are strictly prohibited.** Automatic renewals create open-ended service obligations, may violate APA term caps, deprive Polaris of the ability to reallocate resources to its remaining businesses, and eliminate Polaris\'s leverage to negotiate extension pricing.
102: >
103: > • Extension pricing at cost-plus-15% reflects the additional administrative burden, resource diversion, and opportunity cost of extended service delivery beyond the original contemplated term.
104: 
105: **[3.2 Termination of Individual Services]{.underline}**
106: 
107:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
108:                                       **Position**
109:   ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
110:   **Target**                          Either party may terminate any individual Service upon **90 days\'** prior written notice.
111: 
112:   **Fallback**                        90 days for Service Recipient termination; 60 days for Service Provider termination upon Service Recipient material breach. Service Recipient may terminate on 30 days\' notice if the applicable function has been fully migrated.
113:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
114: 
115: The 90-day notice period is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(c). Do not accept termination notice periods longer than 90 days, as longer periods lock Polaris into service obligations even when continued provision is inefficient or undesirable.
116: 
117: **[3.3 Termination for Cause]{.underline}**
118: 
119:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
120:                                       **Position**
121:   ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
122:   **Target**                          Either party may terminate the entire TSA upon material breach if the breaching party fails to cure within **30 days** of receiving written notice. Service Provider may terminate immediately (no cure period) upon: (i) Service Recipient insolvency or bankruptcy, (ii) failure to pay undisputed invoices for more than 60 days past due, or (iii) conduct creating material legal, regulatory, or reputational risk for Polaris.
123: 
124:   **Fallback**                        Accept 45-day cure period. Maintain immediate termination rights for insolvency and non-payment.
125:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
126: 
127: **[3.4 Termination Assistance / Wind-Down]{.underline}**
128: 
129:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
130:                                       **Position**
131:   ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
132:   **Target**                          Upon expiration or termination of any Service, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for a period not to exceed **60 days** at **cost-plus-15%**. Assistance includes: knowledge transfer, data migration support, cooperation with replacement providers, and transition documentation. No obligation to provide termination assistance if Service Recipient has outstanding unpaid invoices.
133: 
134:   **Fallback**                        Extend termination assistance period to 90 days maximum. Accept cost-plus-10% as absolute floor.
135:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
136: 
137: **Critical Note:** The TSA must include termination assistance provisions. A TSA that is silent on wind-down obligations creates ambiguity regarding Polaris\'s post-termination cooperation obligations and exposes Polaris to claims that implied duties of good faith require indefinite assistance. Affirmatively negotiating a defined, compensated wind-down period protects Polaris by establishing clear boundaries.
138: 
139: **[Section 4: Service Fees and Payment]{.underline}**
140: 
141: **[4.1 Fee Calculation Methodology]{.underline}**
142: 
143:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
144:                                       **Position**
145:   ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
146:   **Target**                          All service fees calculated on a **cost-plus-10%** basis: fully-loaded cost (direct labor, allocated overhead, system costs, out-of-pocket expenses) plus a **uniform 10% markup** across all service categories.
147: 
148:   **Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-7% or cost-plus-8% if buyer pushes back. Never accept a markup below cost-plus-5%.
149:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
150: 
151: **Key Negotiation Points:**
152: 
153: > • The cost-plus-10% cap is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(b). All fee calculations must be verified for compliance with this APA-mandated ceiling.
154: >
155: > • The 10% markup applies **uniformly** to all service categories. There shall be no service category that carries a different (higher or lower) markup percentage. Any deviation from uniform pricing must be flagged.
156: >
157: > • Each Service Schedule must include: (i) base cost components, (ii) estimated monthly cost, (iii) markup percentage, and (iv) resulting monthly fee. A consolidated Fee Schedule should be attached as an exhibit.
158: 
159: **[4.2 Fee Escalation]{.underline}**
160: 
161:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
162:                                       **Position**
163:   ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
164:   **Target**                          Annual escalation (on each anniversary of Closing) by the greater of **(a) 3%** or **(b) CPI-U** for the trailing 12-month period. Additional escalation upon an \"Escalation Event\" (material cost increase due to changes in law/regulation/vendor pricing, or Service Recipient request for material volume/scope increase).
165: 
166:   **Fallback**                        Accept CPI-U only (no 3% floor). Maintain Escalation Event provision.
167:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
168: 
169: **[4.3 Payment Terms]{.underline}**
170: 
171:   --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
172:                                       **Position**
173:   ----------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
174:   **Target**                          Monthly invoicing within 15 business days after month-end. Payment due **Net 30** from date of invoice. Late interest at the lesser of **1.5% per month** or maximum rate permitted by law. Undisputed portions must be paid regardless of disputes over other portions.
175: 
176:   **Fallback**                        Accept Net 45 as maximum. Interest at 1.0%/month as floor.
177:   --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
178: 
179: **Critical Note:** Never accept vague payment language such as *\"payment within a commercially reasonable time\"* or *\"payment to be made promptly.\"* Specific payment terms are essential for cash flow management and enforcement. Vague formulations are unenforceable as a practical matter and create unnecessary disputes.
180: 
181: **[4.4 Change Orders]{.underline}**
182: 
183:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
184:                                       **Position**
185:   ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
186:   **Target**                          Any request for out-of-scope services, material volume increase, or material scope change requires a **written change order** signed by authorized representatives of both parties. Change order pricing: **cost-plus-15%**. Acceptance at Service Provider\'s **sole discretion**. No obligation to perform until change order is fully executed and any required advance payment received.
187: 
188:   **Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-10% for change orders. Maintain written change order requirement, dual signature, and Service Provider discretion.
189:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
190: 
191: **Critical Note:** The TSA must include a formal change order procedure. Without one, Service Recipient can expand scope through informal requests and then argue that expanded services are covered under the existing fee structure. A documented change order process protects Polaris against scope creep and ensures compensation for incremental burden.
192: 
193: **[Section 5: Liability and Indemnification]{.underline}**
194: 
195: **[5.1 Limitation of Liability --- Aggregate Cap]{.underline}**
196: 
197:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
198:                                       **Position**
199:   ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
200:   **Target**                          Service Provider\'s aggregate liability shall not exceed total fees actually paid during the **trailing twelve (12) month period** preceding the date on which the claim first arose.
201: 
202:   **Fallback**                        **APA-mandated; not subject to negotiation.** APA Section 7.12(d) specifies the trailing 12-month fee cap. The TSA must conform.
203:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
204: 
205: **Key Negotiation Points --- Illustrative Exposure Analysis:**
206: 
207: The distinction between a trailing 12-month fee cap and a total-fees (or total-fee-multiple) cap is significant. Using representative assumptions:
208: 
209:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
210:   **Cap Formulation**                  **Calculation**                **Approximate Exposure**
211:   ------------------------------------ ------------------------------ --------------------------
212:   Trailing 12-month fees               \~\$1,122,000/month × 12       **\~\$13,464,000**
213: 
214:   200% of total fees (18-month term)   \~\$1,122,000/month × 18 × 2   **\~\$40,392,000**
215:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
216: 
217: The total-fees formulation creates approximately three times the exposure of the trailing 12-month cap. Reject any liability cap based on total fees paid over the entire term, any multiple thereof, or any fixed dollar amount that exceeds the trailing 12-month fee calculation. The trailing 12-month structure is appropriately calibrated to the ongoing relationship and reflects the APA mandate.
218: 
219: **[5.2 Consequential Damages Waiver]{.underline}**
220: 
221:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
222:                                       **Position**
223:   ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
224:   **Target**                          **MUTUAL** waiver of all consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages (including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, and diminution in value). Exceptions: (i) breaches of confidentiality, (ii) IP infringement, (iii) third-party claim indemnification.
225: 
226:   **Fallback**                        Firm position. Accept narrow additional carve-outs (willful misconduct, fraud). **Never accept a non-mutual waiver.**
227:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
228: 
229: **Critical Note:** The waiver must be **mutual** --- both parties waive claims against the other. A unilateral waiver (where only Service Recipient waives) is insufficient because it leaves Service Provider exposed to potentially unlimited consequential damages claims. As service provider, Polaris\'s consequential damages exposure (e.g., claims for business interruption, lost contracts, or supply chain disruption) could vastly exceed the TSA fee value. The mutual waiver limits both parties to direct damages.
230: 
231: **[5.3 Indemnification]{.underline}**
232: 
233:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
234:                                       **Position**
235:   ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
236:   **Target**                          Service Recipient indemnifies Service Provider against all third-party claims arising from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance upon Services, except to the extent caused by Service Provider\'s **gross negligence or willful misconduct**. Service Provider\'s indemnification limited to third-party claims arising from its gross negligence or willful misconduct. All indemnification subject to the aggregate cap in Section 5.1.
237: 
238:   **Fallback**                        Accept proportionate fault standard. Maintain gross negligence/willful misconduct threshold for Service Provider indemnification.
239:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
240: 
241: **[Section 6: Intellectual Property and Data]{.underline}**
242: 
243: **[6.1 IP Ownership]{.underline}**
244: 
245:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
246:                                       **Position**
247:   ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
248:   **Target**                          All Service Provider IP (proprietary technology, tools, methodologies, templates, software, systems, know-how, and processes) remains the **sole and exclusive property** of Service Provider. **No license, sublicense, right, or interest** granted to Service Recipient. Access ceases immediately upon expiration or termination.
249: 
250:   **Fallback**                        **Firm position. No license grant is acceptable.** If buyer requires specific tools post-transition, address through a separate, independently negotiated license agreement with appropriate restrictions and compensation.
251:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
252: 
253: **Key Negotiation Points:**
254: 
255: > • Reject any license grant --- including non-exclusive, limited, or term-limited licenses --- to Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, templates, or know-how.
256: >
257: > • **Specifically reject** language granting *\"perpetual,\" \"irrevocable,\"* or *\"royalty-free\"* licenses. Such language permanently divests Polaris of exclusive control over its proprietary operational IP.
258: >
259: > • Service Recipient receives no right to use, access, copy, modify, reverse engineer, or create derivative works of any Service Provider IP outside of receiving the Services during the Term.
260: >
261: > • Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, and know-how have been developed over decades and are deployed across all four operating divisions. Any license to a buyer could compromise Polaris\'s competitive position and the value of these assets across Polaris\'s entire enterprise.
262: 
263: **[6.2 Data Ownership and Confidentiality]{.underline}**
264: 
265:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
266:                                       **Position**
267:   ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
268:   **Target**                          Service Provider Data (all data, databases, and information systems owned or operated by Polaris) remains Polaris\'s confidential property. Buyer Data (data relating exclusively to the divested business, generated after Closing) is owned by Service Recipient. Service Provider will cooperate in transferring Buyer Data upon termination. Service Provider systems (including SAP S/4HANA ERP), network infrastructure, and cybersecurity tools remain Service Provider property.
269: 
270:   **Fallback**                        Accept reasonable data separation and migration obligations. Maintain ownership of all pre-Closing data, system-level data, and Service Provider proprietary information.
271:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
272: 
273: **[6.3 Cross-Border Data Privacy (Mexico / LFPDPPP)]{.underline}**
274: 
275:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
276:                                       **Position**
277:   ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
278:   **Target**                          Where Services involve processing personal data of individuals in Mexico (e.g., payroll, HR, benefits for the Monterrey facility), the TSA must include LFPDPPP-compliant provisions addressing: (i) data controller/processor allocation (Service Recipient as controller, Service Provider as processor), (ii) data processing agreement or equivalent contractual terms, (iii) cross-border data transfer consent mechanisms (privacy notices and consent from Mexican employees), (iv) data security obligations, and (v) breach notification requirements.
279: 
280:   **Fallback**                        At minimum, include a general provision requiring compliance with all applicable data privacy laws, expressly referencing the LFPDPPP, and allocate responsibility for obtaining necessary employee consents.
281:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
282: 
283: **Critical Note:** The TSA must not reference only U.S. data privacy laws. Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) imposes distinct requirements including mandatory privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*), consent obligations, and cross-border transfer restrictions. Failure to address these requirements in the TSA exposes both parties to enforcement risk by Mexico\'s INAI (*Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Información y Protección de Datos Personales*).
284: 
285: **[Section 7: Personnel]{.underline}**
286: 
287: **[7.1 Staffing Discretion]{.underline}**
288: 
289:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
290:                                       **Position**
291:   ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
292:   **Target**                          Service Provider has **sole discretion** over staffing, assignment, reassignment, and replacement of all service-providing personnel, including the right to reassign, promote, transfer, or terminate any individual. Service Provider shall maintain reasonably qualified staff sufficient to meet the applicable service standard.
293: 
294:   **Fallback**                        Accept obligation to provide Service Recipient **15 business days\' advance written notice** before reassigning or replacing personnel on a mutually agreed list, together with obligation to assign a reasonably qualified replacement. Reassignment/replacement decisions remain within Service Provider\'s **sole discretion** --- no consent requirement.
295:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
296: 
297: **Key Negotiation Points:**
298: 
299: > • Do not accept \"Key Personnel\" provisions requiring Service Recipient\'s prior written consent for reassignment or replacement of named individuals. Such provisions undermine Polaris\'s operational flexibility, create potential employment law complications (employees cannot be contractually \"locked\" to a specific assignment by a third party), and give the buyer undue influence over Polaris\'s internal HR decisions.
300: >
301: > • Polaris must retain the ability to manage its workforce across all four divisions without requiring third-party approval.
302: 
303: **[7.2 Non-Solicitation of Service Provider Personnel]{.underline}**
304: 
305:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
306:                                       **Position**
307:   ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
308:   **Target**                          During the Term and for **12 months** following termination/expiration, Service Recipient shall not solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any Polaris employee who provided Services, without Polaris\'s prior written consent. Applies to all service-providing employees (not limited to any Key Personnel list). Exceptions: (i) general solicitations not targeting Service Provider personnel, (ii) individuals terminated by Service Provider without cause.
309: 
310:   **Fallback**                        Reduce post-termination period to 6 months (absolute minimum). Maintain restriction during the Term.
311:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
312: 
313: **Critical Note:** The TSA must include a non-solicitation covenant. Without one, the buyer can cherry-pick Polaris\'s most effective employees --- who gain deep familiarity with the buyer\'s operations through the TSA engagement --- depleting Polaris\'s workforce and undermining both TSA performance and Polaris\'s ability to serve its remaining businesses. This provision is a high-priority negotiation item.
314: 
315: **[Section 8: Insurance]{.underline}**
316: 
317: **[8.1 Service Recipient Insurance Requirements]{.underline}**
318: 
319:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
320:                                       **Position**
321:   ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
322:   **Target**                          Service Recipient shall maintain throughout the Term (and for 12 months following expiration/termination): (a) **CGL: \$5M per occurrence / \$5M aggregate**; (b) **Umbrella/Excess: \$5M**; (c) **Workers\' Comp: statutory limits**. Service Provider named as **additional insured** under CGL and Umbrella. All policies include **waiver of subrogation** in favor of Service Provider. Certificates of insurance within 10 business days of Closing and annually thereafter.
323: 
324:   **Fallback**                        Accept \$3M CGL and \$3M Umbrella as absolute minimums. **Never** accept CGL below \$3M, waive the umbrella requirement, or omit the additional insured endorsement.
325:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
326: 
327: Adequate insurance requirements protect Polaris against claims arising from the buyer\'s operations and use of Polaris\'s services and systems. Given the industrial nature of the divested businesses (coatings, chemicals, manufacturing), the risk profile warrants robust coverage. The additional insured endorsement is particularly important as it provides Polaris with direct rights under the buyer\'s policies.
328: 
329: **[Section 9: Audit Rights]{.underline}**
330: 
331: **[9.1 Service Recipient Audit Rights]{.underline}**
332: 
333:   --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
334:                                       **Position**
335:   ----------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
336:   **Target**                          Service Recipient may audit Service Provider\'s fee-related books and records subject to the following parameters:
337: 
338:   --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
339: 
340:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
341:   **Parameter**              **Target Position**                                                                                                    **Fallback Position**
342:   -------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------
343:   **Frequency**              Once per 12-month period                                                                                               Twice per TSA term (not twice per calendar year)
344: 
345:   **Notice**                 30 business days\' prior written notice                                                                                20 business days\' notice (minimum)
346: 
347:   **Timing**                 During Service Provider\'s normal business hours                                                                       Same
348: 
349:   **Cost**                   At Service Recipient\'s sole expense                                                                                   Same; never accept audit at Service Provider\'s expense as default
350: 
351:   **Scope**                  Fee-related records only; excludes proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, and unrelated personnel records   Same; maintain scope limitations
352: 
353:   **Confidentiality**        All audit results confidential; no disclosure to third parties                                                         Same
354: 
355:   **Overcharge Threshold**   If overcharge exceeds 5% for audited period, Service Provider reimburses overcharge and reasonable audit costs         Same
356:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
357: 
358: **Key Negotiation Points:** Excessive or frequent audits are disruptive to Polaris\'s operations. Requiring Polaris to bear audit costs as a default incentivizes frivolous audits. Short notice periods do not allow adequate preparation time and may result in incomplete responses that are then characterized as non-cooperation.

**[NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK]{.underline}**
**Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. --- Service Provider Positions**
**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT**

This document is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work-product doctrine. It contains the legal strategies, negotiation positions, and confidential assessments of Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. and its counsel. Distribution is strictly limited to authorized personnel. Any unauthorized disclosure, copying, or distribution is prohibited and may constitute a waiver of applicable privileges.
**Maintained by:** Legal Department, Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc., 1200 Commonwealth Avenue, Suite 3000, Pittsburgh, PA 15222
**Approved by:** Sharon M. Petrosian, General Counsel
**Last Updated:** January 15, 2025
**Version:** 4.2

**Distribution:** Limited to Polaris Legal Department, CFO (David K. Okafor), CEO (Margaret R. Lindstrom), and outside counsel (Whitfield & Crane LLP, 600 Grant Street, Suite 4800, Pittsburgh, PA 15219; Lead Partner: Victoria S. Andersen)

This Playbook sets forth Polaris\'s preferred and fallback positions for any Transition Services Agreement in which Polaris acts as Service Provider following a divestiture. All positions should be adapted to the specific transaction and governing purchase agreement. Positions marked **\"Target\"** represent Polaris\'s opening/preferred position. Positions marked **\"Fallback\"** represent the maximum acceptable concession, below which escalation to the General Counsel is required.
Right-click to update Table of Contents
**[Section 1: Purpose and Scope of Playbook]{.underline}**

Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. is a diversified industrial conglomerate incorporated in Delaware, with approximately \$3.2 billion in annual revenue across four operating divisions: Advanced Materials, Specialty Coatings, Precision Components, and Industrial Automation. Polaris is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and maintains domestic and international operations including a manufacturing facility in Monterrey, Mexico.

Divestitures of individual business units frequently require Polaris to provide post-closing transition services to buyers. This need arises because Polaris\'s shared-services infrastructure --- encompassing IT, HR/Payroll, Finance/Accounting, Supply Chain/Procurement, Regulatory/EHS, and Treasury/Tax functions --- supports multiple divisions simultaneously through common personnel and integrated systems. Approximately 100 full-time equivalents across these service categories typically support any single division alongside other Polaris businesses. These personnel remain Polaris employees after closing, necessitating a Transition Services Agreement under which Polaris continues to perform certain functions on behalf of the buyer for a defined transition period.
The purpose of this Playbook is to protect Polaris\'s interests as Service Provider by:
> • **(a)** Limiting liability exposure arising from the provision of transition services;
> • **(b)** Preserving Polaris\'s operational flexibility to manage its own workforce and systems;
> • **(c)** Protecting Polaris\'s proprietary intellectual property, systems, and know-how;
> • **(d)** Ensuring adequate compensation for the administrative burden and resource diversion inherent in service delivery; and
> • **(e)** Maintaining compliance with the terms and constraints set forth in the governing purchase agreement.

This Playbook should always be read in conjunction with the applicable Asset Purchase Agreement (or Stock Purchase Agreement, as applicable). Where the APA mandates specific TSA terms --- including service standard, term, fee cap, or liability structure --- the APA controls and those terms are not subject to further negotiation in the TSA. The Playbook serves as the benchmark against which any buyer\'s draft TSA is evaluated, and any deviation from the positions stated herein should be flagged, analyzed, and escalated as appropriate.
**[Section 2: Service Standard]{.underline}**
**[2.1 Standard of Performance]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Services shall be provided *\"in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality provided to the Business during the twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date.\"* No obligation to exceed historical service levels. No obligation to prioritize Service Recipient over Polaris\'s own internal business needs.
**Fallback**                        Add *\"using commercially reasonable efforts\"* after *\"substantially consistent\"* language. This is the maximum concession.
**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • **Lookback Period:** The lookback period is twelve (12) months prior to the Closing Date. Do not accept a 24-month or longer lookback period. A longer lookback may capture atypical service levels (e.g., pre-pandemic staffing, special project surges) that are not representative of current operations.

> • **\"Substantially Consistent\" Language:** The operative standard is *\"substantially consistent with,\"* which permits reasonable variation. Reject language such as *\"equal to or better than,\"* *\"at least equal to,\"* or *\"no less favorable than.\"* These formulations impose a floor that ratchets upward and does not permit any reduction or variation, however reasonable.

> • **Reject \"Best Practices\" and Similar Standards:** References to *\"industry best practices,\"* *\"commercially reasonable best efforts,\"* or other aspirational benchmarks must be rejected. These terms are undefined, subjective, invite disputes, and impose a standard that may materially exceed what Polaris historically provided to the divested business. Polaris is not a third-party service provider competing for business --- it is providing transitional support as an accommodation.

> • **Not a Guarantor:** Service Provider\'s obligation is limited to making available the same general type and level of resources as historically deployed. Service Provider does not guarantee specific outcomes, results, or service levels beyond what was historically provided.
> • **APA Precedence:** If the APA specifies a service standard (e.g., in the TSA covenant section or an exhibit), that APA standard controls and the TSA cannot impose a more stringent requirement.
**[2.2 Exclusions from Service Obligation]{.underline}**
Service Provider has no obligation to:
> • **(a)** Provide services not described in the applicable Service Schedules;
> • **(b)** Hire additional personnel or acquire additional resources beyond those in place as of the Closing Date;
> • **(c)** Provide services that would violate applicable law or regulation;
> • **(d)** Provide services that would breach any third-party agreement to which Polaris is a party (including software licenses, vendor contracts, or confidentiality agreements);
> • **(e)** Provide advice of any kind --- legal, tax, financial, or strategic.

Service Provider may modify the manner of delivering services to the extent such modifications are consistent with changes made to services provided to Polaris\'s own businesses (e.g., system upgrades, vendor changes, process improvements applied company-wide).
**[Section 3: Term and Termination]{.underline}**
**[3.1 Maximum Term]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Fixed term not to exceed **18 months** from the Closing Date. Hard stop. No automatic renewal. Extensions require: (i) mutual written agreement, (ii) pricing at cost-plus-15%, (iii) maximum extension of 6 months (total possible term: 24 months only upon mutual agreement).
**Fallback**                        Mutual written extension option at cost-plus-10% (minimum). Never accept automatic renewals.
**Key Negotiation Points:**
> • The 18-month maximum is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12 in standard Polaris deals. The TSA cannot exceed the APA-mandated term.

> • **Automatic renewal provisions are strictly prohibited.** Automatic renewals create open-ended service obligations, may violate APA term caps, deprive Polaris of the ability to reallocate resources to its remaining businesses, and eliminate Polaris\'s leverage to negotiate extension pricing.
> • Extension pricing at cost-plus-15% reflects the additional administrative burden, resource diversion, and opportunity cost of extended service delivery beyond the original contemplated term.
**[3.2 Termination of Individual Services]{.underline}**
**Position**
**Target**                          Either party may terminate any individual Service upon **90 days\'** prior written notice.

**Fallback**                        90 days for Service Recipient termination; 60 days for Service Provider termination upon Service Recipient material breach. Service Recipient may terminate on 30 days\' notice if the applicable function has been fully migrated.

The 90-day notice period is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(c). Do not accept termination notice periods longer than 90 days, as longer periods lock Polaris into service obligations even when continued provision is inefficient or undesirable.
**[3.3 Termination for Cause]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Either party may terminate the entire TSA upon material breach if the breaching party fails to cure within **30 days** of receiving written notice. Service Provider may terminate immediately (no cure period) upon: (i) Service Recipient insolvency or bankruptcy, (ii) failure to pay undisputed invoices for more than 60 days past due, or (iii) conduct creating material legal, regulatory, or reputational risk for Polaris.
**Fallback**                        Accept 45-day cure period. Maintain immediate termination rights for insolvency and non-payment.
**[3.4 Termination Assistance / Wind-Down]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Upon expiration or termination of any Service, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for a period not to exceed **60 days** at **cost-plus-15%**. Assistance includes: knowledge transfer, data migration support, cooperation with replacement providers, and transition documentation. No obligation to provide termination assistance if Service Recipient has outstanding unpaid invoices.
**Fallback**                        Extend termination assistance period to 90 days maximum. Accept cost-plus-10% as absolute floor.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include termination assistance provisions. A TSA that is silent on wind-down obligations creates ambiguity regarding Polaris\'s post-termination cooperation obligations and exposes Polaris to claims that implied duties of good faith require indefinite assistance. Affirmatively negotiating a defined, compensated wind-down period protects Polaris by establishing clear boundaries.
**[Section 4: Service Fees and Payment]{.underline}**
**[4.1 Fee Calculation Methodology]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          All service fees calculated on a **cost-plus-10%** basis: fully-loaded cost (direct labor, allocated overhead, system costs, out-of-pocket expenses) plus a **uniform 10% markup** across all service categories.
**Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-7% or cost-plus-8% if buyer pushes back. Never accept a markup below cost-plus-5%.
**Key Negotiation Points:**
> • The cost-plus-10% cap is typically mandated by APA Section 7.12(b). All fee calculations must be verified for compliance with this APA-mandated ceiling.

> • The 10% markup applies **uniformly** to all service categories. There shall be no service category that carries a different (higher or lower) markup percentage. Any deviation from uniform pricing must be flagged.

> • Each Service Schedule must include: (i) base cost components, (ii) estimated monthly cost, (iii) markup percentage, and (iv) resulting monthly fee. A consolidated Fee Schedule should be attached as an exhibit.
**[4.2 Fee Escalation]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Annual escalation (on each anniversary of Closing) by the greater of **(a) 3%** or **(b) CPI-U** for the trailing 12-month period. Additional escalation upon an \"Escalation Event\" (material cost increase due to changes in law/regulation/vendor pricing, or Service Recipient request for material volume/scope increase).
**Fallback**                        Accept CPI-U only (no 3% floor). Maintain Escalation Event provision.
**[4.3 Payment Terms]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Monthly invoicing within 15 business days after month-end. Payment due **Net 30** from date of invoice. Late interest at the lesser of **1.5% per month** or maximum rate permitted by law. Undisputed portions must be paid regardless of disputes over other portions.
**Fallback**                        Accept Net 45 as maximum. Interest at 1.0%/month as floor.

**Critical Note:** Never accept vague payment language such as *\"payment within a commercially reasonable time\"* or *\"payment to be made promptly.\"* Specific payment terms are essential for cash flow management and enforcement. Vague formulations are unenforceable as a practical matter and create unnecessary disputes.
**[4.4 Change Orders]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Any request for out-of-scope services, material volume increase, or material scope change requires a **written change order** signed by authorized representatives of both parties. Change order pricing: **cost-plus-15%**. Acceptance at Service Provider\'s **sole discretion**. No obligation to perform until change order is fully executed and any required advance payment received.
**Fallback**                        Accept cost-plus-10% for change orders. Maintain written change order requirement, dual signature, and Service Provider discretion.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include a formal change order procedure. Without one, Service Recipient can expand scope through informal requests and then argue that expanded services are covered under the existing fee structure. A documented change order process protects Polaris against scope creep and ensures compensation for incremental burden.
**[Section 5: Liability and Indemnification]{.underline}**
**[5.1 Limitation of Liability --- Aggregate Cap]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Provider\'s aggregate liability shall not exceed total fees actually paid during the **trailing twelve (12) month period** preceding the date on which the claim first arose.
**Fallback**                        **APA-mandated; not subject to negotiation.** APA Section 7.12(d) specifies the trailing 12-month fee cap. The TSA must conform.
**Key Negotiation Points --- Illustrative Exposure Analysis:**
The distinction between a trailing 12-month fee cap and a total-fees (or total-fee-multiple) cap is significant. Using representative assumptions:
**Cap Formulation**                  **Calculation**                **Approximate Exposure**

The total-fees formulation creates approximately three times the exposure of the trailing 12-month cap. Reject any liability cap based on total fees paid over the entire term, any multiple thereof, or any fixed dollar amount that exceeds the trailing 12-month fee calculation. The trailing 12-month structure is appropriately calibrated to the ongoing relationship and reflects the APA mandate.
**[5.2 Consequential Damages Waiver]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          **MUTUAL** waiver of all consequential, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, and indirect damages (including lost profits, lost revenue, loss of business opportunity, and diminution in value). Exceptions: (i) breaches of confidentiality, (ii) IP infringement, (iii) third-party claim indemnification.
**Fallback**                        Firm position. Accept narrow additional carve-outs (willful misconduct, fraud). **Never accept a non-mutual waiver.**

**Critical Note:** The waiver must be **mutual** --- both parties waive claims against the other. A unilateral waiver (where only Service Recipient waives) is insufficient because it leaves Service Provider exposed to potentially unlimited consequential damages claims. As service provider, Polaris\'s consequential damages exposure (e.g., claims for business interruption, lost contracts, or supply chain disruption) could vastly exceed the TSA fee value. The mutual waiver limits both parties to direct damages.
**[5.3 Indemnification]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Recipient indemnifies Service Provider against all third-party claims arising from Service Recipient\'s use of or reliance upon Services, except to the extent caused by Service Provider\'s **gross negligence or willful misconduct**. Service Provider\'s indemnification limited to third-party claims arising from its gross negligence or willful misconduct. All indemnification subject to the aggregate cap in Section 5.1.
**Fallback**                        Accept proportionate fault standard. Maintain gross negligence/willful misconduct threshold for Service Provider indemnification.
**[Section 6: Intellectual Property and Data]{.underline}**
**[6.1 IP Ownership]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          All Service Provider IP (proprietary technology, tools, methodologies, templates, software, systems, know-how, and processes) remains the **sole and exclusive property** of Service Provider. **No license, sublicense, right, or interest** granted to Service Recipient. Access ceases immediately upon expiration or termination.

**Fallback**                        **Firm position. No license grant is acceptable.** If buyer requires specific tools post-transition, address through a separate, independently negotiated license agreement with appropriate restrictions and compensation.
**Key Negotiation Points:**
> • Reject any license grant --- including non-exclusive, limited, or term-limited licenses --- to Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, templates, or know-how.

> • **Specifically reject** language granting *\"perpetual,\" \"irrevocable,\"* or *\"royalty-free\"* licenses. Such language permanently divests Polaris of exclusive control over its proprietary operational IP.
> • Service Recipient receives no right to use, access, copy, modify, reverse engineer, or create derivative works of any Service Provider IP outside of receiving the Services during the Term.

> • Polaris\'s tools, methodologies, and know-how have been developed over decades and are deployed across all four operating divisions. Any license to a buyer could compromise Polaris\'s competitive position and the value of these assets across Polaris\'s entire enterprise.
**[6.2 Data Ownership and Confidentiality]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Provider Data (all data, databases, and information systems owned or operated by Polaris) remains Polaris\'s confidential property. Buyer Data (data relating exclusively to the divested business, generated after Closing) is owned by Service Recipient. Service Provider will cooperate in transferring Buyer Data upon termination. Service Provider systems (including SAP S/4HANA ERP), network infrastructure, and cybersecurity tools remain Service Provider property.

**Fallback**                        Accept reasonable data separation and migration obligations. Maintain ownership of all pre-Closing data, system-level data, and Service Provider proprietary information.
**[6.3 Cross-Border Data Privacy (Mexico / LFPDPPP)]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Where Services involve processing personal data of individuals in Mexico (e.g., payroll, HR, benefits for the Monterrey facility), the TSA must include LFPDPPP-compliant provisions addressing: (i) data controller/processor allocation (Service Recipient as controller, Service Provider as processor), (ii) data processing agreement or equivalent contractual terms, (iii) cross-border data transfer consent mechanisms (privacy notices and consent from Mexican employees), (iv) data security obligations, and (v) breach notification requirements.

**Fallback**                        At minimum, include a general provision requiring compliance with all applicable data privacy laws, expressly referencing the LFPDPPP, and allocate responsibility for obtaining necessary employee consents.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must not reference only U.S. data privacy laws. Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) imposes distinct requirements including mandatory privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*), consent obligations, and cross-border transfer restrictions. Failure to address these requirements in the TSA exposes both parties to enforcement risk by Mexico\'s INAI (*Instituto Nacional de Transparencia, Acceso a la Información y Protección de Datos Personales*).
**[Section 7: Personnel]{.underline}**
**[7.1 Staffing Discretion]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Provider has **sole discretion** over staffing, assignment, reassignment, and replacement of all service-providing personnel, including the right to reassign, promote, transfer, or terminate any individual. Service Provider shall maintain reasonably qualified staff sufficient to meet the applicable service standard.

**Fallback**                        Accept obligation to provide Service Recipient **15 business days\' advance written notice** before reassigning or replacing personnel on a mutually agreed list, together with obligation to assign a reasonably qualified replacement. Reassignment/replacement decisions remain within Service Provider\'s **sole discretion** --- no consent requirement.
**Key Negotiation Points:**

> • Do not accept \"Key Personnel\" provisions requiring Service Recipient\'s prior written consent for reassignment or replacement of named individuals. Such provisions undermine Polaris\'s operational flexibility, create potential employment law complications (employees cannot be contractually \"locked\" to a specific assignment by a third party), and give the buyer undue influence over Polaris\'s internal HR decisions.
> • Polaris must retain the ability to manage its workforce across all four divisions without requiring third-party approval.
**[7.2 Non-Solicitation of Service Provider Personnel]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          During the Term and for **12 months** following termination/expiration, Service Recipient shall not solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any Polaris employee who provided Services, without Polaris\'s prior written consent. Applies to all service-providing employees (not limited to any Key Personnel list). Exceptions: (i) general solicitations not targeting Service Provider personnel, (ii) individuals terminated by Service Provider without cause.
**Fallback**                        Reduce post-termination period to 6 months (absolute minimum). Maintain restriction during the Term.

**Critical Note:** The TSA must include a non-solicitation covenant. Without one, the buyer can cherry-pick Polaris\'s most effective employees --- who gain deep familiarity with the buyer\'s operations through the TSA engagement --- depleting Polaris\'s workforce and undermining both TSA performance and Polaris\'s ability to serve its remaining businesses. This provision is a high-priority negotiation item.
**[Section 8: Insurance]{.underline}**
**[8.1 Service Recipient Insurance Requirements]{.underline}**
**Position**

**Target**                          Service Recipient shall maintain throughout the Term (and for 12 months following expiration/termination): (a) **CGL: \$5M per occurrence / \$5M aggregate**; (b) **Umbrella/Excess: \$5M**; (c) **Workers\' Comp: statutory limits**. Service Provider named as **additional insured** under CGL and Umbrella. All policies include **waiver of subrogation** in favor of Service Provider. Certificates of insurance within 10 business days of Closing and annually thereafter.

**Fallback**                        Accept \$3M CGL and \$3M Umbrella as absolute minimums. **Never** accept CGL below \$3M, waive the umbrella requirement, or omit the additional insured endorsement.

Adequate insurance requirements protect Polaris against claims arising from the buyer\'s operations and use of Polaris\'s services and systems. Given the industrial nature of the divested businesses (coatings, chemicals, manufacturing), the risk profile warrants robust coverage. The additional insured endorsement is particularly important as it provides Polaris with direct rights under the buyer\'s policies.
**[Section 9: Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**[9.1 Service Recipient Audit Rights]{.underline}**
**Position**
**Target**                          Service Recipient may audit Service Provider\'s fee-related books and records subject to the following parameters:
**Parameter**              **Target Position**                                                                                                    **Fallback Position**
**Frequency**              Once per 12-month period                                                                                               Twice per TSA term (not twice per calendar year)
**Notice**                 30 business days\' prior written notice                                                                                20 business days\' notice (minimum)
**Timing**                 During Service Provider\'s normal business hours                                                                       Same

**Cost**                   At Service Recipient\'s sole expense                                                                                   Same; never accept audit at Service Provider\'s expense as default
**Scope**                  Fee-related records only; excludes proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, and unrelated personnel records   Same; maintain scope limitations
**Confidentiality**        All audit results confidential; no disclosure to third parties                                                         Same
**Overcharge Threshold**   If overcharge exceeds 5% for audited period, Service Provider reimburses overcharge and reasonable audit costs         Same

**Key Negotiation Points:** Excessive or frequent audits are disruptive to Polaris\'s operations. Requiring Polaris to bear audit costs as a default incentivizes frivolous audits. Short notice periods do not allow adequate preparation time and may result in incomplete responses that are then characterized as non-cooperation.
**[Section 10: Force Majeure]{.underline}**
**[10.1 Force Majeure Events]{.underline}**

49: As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

51: \"**Acquired Assets**\" means all of the assets, properties, and rights of every kind and nature, whether real, personal, or mixed, tangible or intangible, owned, leased, licensed, or used by Seller primarily in connection with the Business, including without limitation: (i) the Facilities; (ii) all machinery, equipment, tools, furniture, fixtures, supplies, vehicles, and other tangible personal property set forth on Schedule 2.1(a) or otherwise used primarily in the Business; (iii) all Inventory; (iv) all Transferred Intellectual Property; (v) all Assumed Contracts; (vi) all Permits; (vii) all books, records, and files, in whatever form or medium, to the extent primarily relating to the Business; and (viii) all goodwill associated with the Business. For purposes of calculating Fully-Loaded Cost, Seller shall not include any costs or expenses attributable to services or personnel that are not reasonably allocable to the Transition Service in question.

63: \"**IMMEX Program**\" means the Mexican Maquiladora and Export Services Industry Program (*Industria Manufacturera, Maquiladora y de Servicios de Exportación*) established under Mexico\'s Decree for the Promotion of the Manufacturing, Maquiladora and Export Services Industry, as amended from time to time, and all implementing rules, regulations, and official standards issued thereunder.

103: **[Section 7.12 --- Transition Services Agreement]{.underline}**

105: **Section 7.12(a) --- Obligation to Enter into TSA**
106: 
107: At or prior to the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall negotiate in good faith and enter into a Transition Services Agreement, on commercially reasonable terms and conditions, pursuant to which Seller shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Buyer (or its applicable Affiliates) the Transition Services described in Exhibit H hereto for a transition period following the Closing Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"). The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.
108: 
109: The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.
110: 
111: For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.
112: 
113: The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.
