115: **Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**
116: 
117: All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.
118: 
119: The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.
120: 
121: In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.
122: 
123: Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.
124: 
125: **Section 7.12(c) --- Termination of Individual Services**
126: 
127: Buyer or Seller may terminate any individual Transition Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other party, specifying the Transition Service to be terminated and the effective date of such termination. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.1 of this Agreement.
128: 
129: Upon termination of any individual Transition Service, Buyer\'s obligation to pay TSA Fees with respect to such terminated Transition Service shall cease as of the effective date of termination, subject to Buyer\'s obligation to pay all TSA Fees accrued through such effective date and to reimburse Seller for any non-cancelable costs or commitments that Seller incurred prior to receipt of the termination notice in reasonable reliance on the continuation of such Transition Service, provided that Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such non-cancelable costs.
130: 
131: Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Transition Services Agreement provides for a notice period different from the ninety (90) day period specified in this Section 7.12(c), the notice period set forth in this Agreement shall control. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Section 7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to the termination of individual Transition Services, and any provision in the Transition Services Agreement purporting to require a longer or shorter notice period shall be of no force or effect.
132: 
133: **Section 7.12(d) --- Limitation of Liability**
134: 
135: The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that the aggregate liability of the Service Provider (and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents) to the Service Recipient under or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient to the Service Provider during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient (the \"**TSA Liability Cap**\").
136: 
137: For purposes of calculating the TSA Liability Cap during the first twelve (12) months of the Transition Period, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated based on the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient from the Closing Date through the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient. Thereafter, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated on a rolling twelve (12) month basis, measured from the date of assertion of the applicable claim and looking back twelve (12) months from such date.
138: 
139: The limitation set forth in this Section 7.12(d) shall not apply to:
140: 
141: > \(i\) claims arising from a party\'s fraud or willful misconduct;
142: >
143: > \(ii\) a party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations under the Transition Services Agreement; or
144: >
145: > \(iii\) a party\'s indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims arising out of the provision or receipt of Transition Services, to the extent such third-party claims result from the indemnifying party\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.
146: 
147: In no event shall either party be liable to the other party for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory, and regardless of whether such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages; provided, however, that this sentence shall not limit the liability of a party with respect to third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under the Transition Services Agreement.
148: 
149: The parties acknowledge and agree that the foregoing limitations on liability reflect the parties\' agreement regarding the allocation of risk under the Transition Services Agreement, and that neither party would have entered into this Agreement without such limitations.

151: **Section 7.12(e) --- Cooperation**
152: 
153: During the Transition Period, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own capability to perform the Transition Services independently and to reduce its reliance on Seller for the provision of such Transition Services as promptly as reasonably practicable. Buyer shall dedicate appropriate internal resources, including qualified personnel and financial resources, to the transition effort and shall develop and implement a transition plan in consultation with Seller.
154: 
155: Seller shall cooperate in good faith with Buyer\'s efforts to transition the Transition Services to Buyer\'s own systems, personnel, and third-party providers. Such cooperation shall include reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation of processes and procedures, and making Seller\'s personnel reasonably available for consultations during normal business hours.
156: 
157: Nothing in this Section 7.12 or the Transition Services Agreement shall require Seller to:
158: 
159: > \(i\) maintain any employee in employment or any contractor engagement solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services;
160: >
161: > \(ii\) acquire, license, or maintain any hardware, software, or other technology solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services, except to the extent that Seller was licensing or maintaining such technology for the benefit of the Business as of the Closing Date and the cost of such license or maintenance is included in the Fully-Loaded Cost;
162: >
163: > \(iii\) provide any Transition Service in a manner that would require Seller to violate any applicable Law or breach any contractual obligation to a third party; or
164: >
165: > \(iv\) disclose any trade secrets, proprietary information, or confidential business information of Seller that does not relate to the Business.

167: **Section 7.12(f) --- Service Standard; No Prioritization**
168: 
169: The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that Seller shall provide the Transition Services in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. The parties acknowledge that Seller\'s historical practices, methodologies, systems, and resource levels as applied to the Business during such twelve (12) month period shall serve as the benchmark for the required level of service under the Transition Services Agreement.
170: 
171: Nothing in the Transition Services Agreement shall obligate Seller to provide Transition Services at a level of quality, timeliness, or responsiveness that exceeds the level provided to the Business during such twelve (12) month period, or to prioritize the provision of Transition Services over services that Seller provides for its own account, for its retained business divisions, or for its other business units. Seller shall not be required to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices in connection with the provision of Transition Services that were not in use with respect to the Business during such twelve (12) month period.
172: 
173: The parties acknowledge and agree that Seller is not a professional services provider and that the Transition Services are being provided on an accommodation basis to facilitate the orderly transition of the Business to Buyer. Accordingly, the parties agree that the standard of care applicable to the provision of Transition Services shall be measured solely by reference to Seller\'s historical performance with respect to the Business and shall not be measured against any external industry standard, best-practice benchmark, or professional services standard.

365: **Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$95,000

367: **Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$104,500

This ASSET PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this \"**Agreement**\") is entered into as of March 14, 2025, by and between:
**POLARIS INDUSTRIAL HOLDINGS, INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices at 1200 Commonwealth Avenue, Suite 3000, Pittsburgh, PA 15222 (\"**Seller**\"),
and
**TRIDENT MANUFACTURING GROUP, INC.**, an Ohio corporation, with its principal offices at 800 Lakeside Drive, Suite 400, Cleveland, OH 44114 (\"**Buyer**\").
**RECITALS**
**WHEREAS:**

\(A\) Seller operates, among other businesses, the Specialty Coatings Division (as defined below), which is engaged in the development, manufacture, distribution, and sale of specialty industrial coatings and related products throughout the United States, Mexico, and internationally;

**[Section 7.12 --- Transition Services Agreement]{.underline}**
**Section 7.12(a) --- Obligation to Enter into TSA**

At or prior to the Closing, Seller and Buyer shall negotiate in good faith and enter into a Transition Services Agreement, on commercially reasonable terms and conditions, pursuant to which Seller shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Buyer (or its applicable Affiliates) the Transition Services described in Exhibit H hereto for a transition period following the Closing Date (the \"**Transition Period**\"). The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.

The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.

The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.
**Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**

All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.

The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.

In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.

Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.
**Section 7.12(c) --- Termination of Individual Services**

Buyer or Seller may terminate any individual Transition Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other party, specifying the Transition Service to be terminated and the effective date of such termination. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.1 of this Agreement.

Upon termination of any individual Transition Service, Buyer\'s obligation to pay TSA Fees with respect to such terminated Transition Service shall cease as of the effective date of termination, subject to Buyer\'s obligation to pay all TSA Fees accrued through such effective date and to reimburse Seller for any non-cancelable costs or commitments that Seller incurred prior to receipt of the termination notice in reasonable reliance on the continuation of such Transition Service, provided that Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such non-cancelable costs.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Transition Services Agreement provides for a notice period different from the ninety (90) day period specified in this Section 7.12(c), the notice period set forth in this Agreement shall control. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Section 7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to the termination of individual Transition Services, and any provision in the Transition Services Agreement purporting to require a longer or shorter notice period shall be of no force or effect.
**Section 7.12(d) --- Limitation of Liability**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that the aggregate liability of the Service Provider (and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents) to the Service Recipient under or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient to the Service Provider during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient (the \"**TSA Liability Cap**\").

For purposes of calculating the TSA Liability Cap during the first twelve (12) months of the Transition Period, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated based on the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient from the Closing Date through the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient. Thereafter, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated on a rolling twelve (12) month basis, measured from the date of assertion of the applicable claim and looking back twelve (12) months from such date.
The limitation set forth in this Section 7.12(d) shall not apply to:
> \(i\) claims arising from a party\'s fraud or willful misconduct;
> \(ii\) a party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations under the Transition Services Agreement; or

> \(iii\) a party\'s indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims arising out of the provision or receipt of Transition Services, to the extent such third-party claims result from the indemnifying party\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.

In no event shall either party be liable to the other party for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory, and regardless of whether such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages; provided, however, that this sentence shall not limit the liability of a party with respect to third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under the Transition Services Agreement.

The parties acknowledge and agree that the foregoing limitations on liability reflect the parties\' agreement regarding the allocation of risk under the Transition Services Agreement, and that neither party would have entered into this Agreement without such limitations.
**Section 7.12(e) --- Cooperation**

During the Transition Period, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own capability to perform the Transition Services independently and to reduce its reliance on Seller for the provision of such Transition Services as promptly as reasonably practicable. Buyer shall dedicate appropriate internal resources, including qualified personnel and financial resources, to the transition effort and shall develop and implement a transition plan in consultation with Seller.

Seller shall cooperate in good faith with Buyer\'s efforts to transition the Transition Services to Buyer\'s own systems, personnel, and third-party providers. Such cooperation shall include reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation of processes and procedures, and making Seller\'s personnel reasonably available for consultations during normal business hours.
Nothing in this Section 7.12 or the Transition Services Agreement shall require Seller to:
> \(i\) maintain any employee in employment or any contractor engagement solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services;

> \(ii\) acquire, license, or maintain any hardware, software, or other technology solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services, except to the extent that Seller was licensing or maintaining such technology for the benefit of the Business as of the Closing Date and the cost of such license or maintenance is included in the Fully-Loaded Cost;
> \(iii\) provide any Transition Service in a manner that would require Seller to violate any applicable Law or breach any contractual obligation to a third party; or
> \(iv\) disclose any trade secrets, proprietary information, or confidential business information of Seller that does not relate to the Business.
**Section 7.12(f) --- Service Standard; No Prioritization**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that Seller shall provide the Transition Services in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. The parties acknowledge that Seller\'s historical practices, methodologies, systems, and resource levels as applied to the Business during such twelve (12) month period shall serve as the benchmark for the required level of service under the Transition Services Agreement.

Nothing in the Transition Services Agreement shall obligate Seller to provide Transition Services at a level of quality, timeliness, or responsiveness that exceeds the level provided to the Business during such twelve (12) month period, or to prioritize the provision of Transition Services over services that Seller provides for its own account, for its retained business divisions, or for its other business units. Seller shall not be required to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices in connection with the provision of Transition Services that were not in use with respect to the Business during such twelve (12) month period.

The parties acknowledge and agree that Seller is not a professional services provider and that the Transition Services are being provided on an accommodation basis to facilitate the orderly transition of the Business to Buyer. Accordingly, the parties agree that the standard of care applicable to the provision of Transition Services shall be measured solely by reference to Seller\'s historical performance with respect to the Business and shall not be measured against any external industry standard, best-practice benchmark, or professional services standard.
**Section 7.12(g) --- Cross-Border Services**

To the extent that any Transition Services are provided in connection with the operations of the Monterrey Facility or involve the processing of personal data of employees located in Mexico, the Transition Services Agreement shall include commercially reasonable provisions to ensure compliance with applicable Mexican Law, including:

> \(i\) the IMMEX Program requirements applicable to the Monterrey Facility, including provisions addressing the maintenance of the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification, the allocation of responsibility for IMMEX reporting obligations during the Transition Period, and compliance with applicable customs and trade requirements; and

> \(ii\) Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) and its Regulations, including provisions addressing the lawful basis for the transfer and processing of personal data of Monterrey Facility employees, the implementation of appropriate privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*), and the establishment of adequate data protection safeguards.

Seller and Buyer shall cooperate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of responsibilities under the IMMEX Program during the Transition Period, including with respect to the maintenance of the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification, the timely filing of all required IMMEX reports, and the management of temporary importation records. The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the transition of IMMEX Program obligations from Seller to Buyer is completed in a manner that avoids any lapse in the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification or any violation of applicable Mexican customs Law.

lines.text: **SCHEDULE B** **INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following information technology services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **ERP System Access and Support.** Continued access to and support of Service Provider\'s SAP S/4HANA enterprise resource planning system for the Business, including the following modules: Finance (FI/CO), Materials Management (MM), Sales and Distribution (SD), Production Planning (PP), Quality Management (QM), and Plant Maintenance (PM). Service Provider shall maintain the system in operational condition, apply necessary patches and updates in accordance with its standard maintenance schedule, and provide Tier 2 and Tier 3 SAP application support for Business users.

> \(b\) **Network Infrastructure Support.** Management and maintenance of the wide area network (WAN), local area network (LAN), and virtual private network (VPN) infrastructure supporting the Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; Greenville, South Carolina; and Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico facilities, to the extent such infrastructure is shared with or provided by Service Provider. This includes router and switch management, bandwidth monitoring, and connectivity to Service Provider\'s data center.

> \(c\) **Cybersecurity Monitoring and Incident Response.** Monitoring of the Business\'s IT environment for cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents using Service Provider\'s existing security information and event management (SIEM) platform, endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools, and intrusion detection systems. In the event of a cybersecurity incident that affects or reasonably could be expected to affect Business data, Service Provider shall notify Service Recipient within seventy-two (72) hours of Service Provider\'s becoming aware of such incident and shall cooperate with Service Recipient in investigating and remediating the incident.

> \(d\) **IT Help Desk Support.** Tier 1 and Tier 2 IT help desk support for Business users, available during normal business hours (8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. local time at each facility, Monday through Friday, excluding holidays). Service Provider shall maintain a ticketing system for tracking and resolving help desk requests and shall provide monthly summary reports on ticket volume, resolution times, and open issues.

> \(e\) **Email and Collaboration Tools.** Continued access to Service Provider\'s Microsoft 365 environment, including Exchange Online (email), SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, and Microsoft Teams, for Business users. Service Provider shall maintain user accounts, distribution lists, and shared mailboxes for the Business during the Service Period.

> \(f\) **Data Backup and Disaster Recovery.** Data backup services for Business data stored on Service Provider\'s systems, including daily incremental backups and weekly full backups. Service Provider shall maintain disaster recovery capabilities consistent with its existing disaster recovery plan and shall include the Business\'s critical systems and data in such plan during the Service Period.
**2. Service Provider Personnel**
Service Provider shall assign approximately thirty-one (31) full-time equivalent personnel to provide the Information Technology Services, including the following roles:

IT Director                         1
Senior Systems Administrators       4
SAP Basis Administrators            3
Network Engineers                   5
Cybersecurity Analysts              3
Help Desk Technicians               8

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path('/home/agarwaldi/dsh-bench-harness/runs/hv-mixed200-lunahigh-flip-r7-20261118T030322Z/tasks/corporate-ma__draft-markup-of-transition-services-agreement-tsa/workspace')
OUT = ROOT/'output'
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
SRC = ROOT/'documents/trident-draft-tsa.docx'

RED = 'C00000'; BLUE = '0000FF'; GOLD = 'FFF2CC'; LIGHTBLUE = 'EAF3FF'; GRAY='666666'; DARK='1F4E79'

# ---------- helpers ----------
def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    borders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if borders is None:
        borders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(borders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge); element = borders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag); borders.append(element)
            for k,v in kwargs[edge].items(): element.set(qn('w:'+k), str(v))

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(tblHeader)

def set_cell_text(cell, text, bold=False, color=None, size=9):
    cell.text = ''
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    r = p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.font.size=Pt(size)
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    cell.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER

def add_field_run(p, label, value, color='000000'):
    r=p.add_run(label); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    r=p.add_run(value); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)

def add_comment_after(doc, anchor, cid, priority, basis, risk, position):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.style = doc.styles['Comment Callout']
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.35)
    p.paragraph_format.right_indent = Inches(0.15)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
    run=p.add_run(f'SELLER COMMENT {cid} — {priority.upper()}\n'); run.bold=True; run.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
    for lab,val in [('Basis: ',basis),('Risk to Polaris: ',risk),('Position: ',position)]:
        rr=p.add_run(lab); rr.bold=True; rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
        rr=p.add_run(val+'\n' if lab!='Position: ' else val); rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string('333333')
    # light shading and left border
    pPr=p._p.get_or_add_pPr(); shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), GOLD); pPr.append(shd)
    pBdr=OxmlElement('w:pBdr'); left=OxmlElement('w:left'); left.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); left.set(qn('w:sz'),'18'); left.set(qn('w:space'),'6'); left.set(qn('w:color'), DARK); pBdr.append(left); pPr.append(pBdr)
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    return p

def insert_para_after(doc, anchor, text, style='Normal', color=None, bold=False, underline=False, strike=False):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.style=style
    r=p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.font.size=Pt(9.5)
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    r.underline=underline; r.strike=strike
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    return p

def redline_para(p, old, new, heading=False):
    p.clear()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    r=p.add_run(old); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); r.font.strike=True
    r=p.add_run('\n'); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    r=p.add_run(new); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE); r.font.underline=True

def find_para(doc, startswith):
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if p.text.strip().startswith(startswith): return p
    raise KeyError(startswith)

def add_comment_for_prefix(doc, prefix, cid, priority, basis, risk, position):
    p=find_para(doc,prefix); add_comment_after(doc,p,cid,priority,basis,risk,position); return p

def style_doc(doc):
    styles=doc.styles
    normal=styles['Normal']; normal.font.name='Arial'; normal.font.size=Pt(9.5)
    for name in ['Heading 1','Heading 2','Heading 3']:
        st=styles[name]; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
    if 'Comment Callout' not in styles:
        st=styles.add_style('Comment Callout', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
        st.base_style=styles['Normal']; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    # footer
    for sec in doc.sections:
        f=sec.footer.paragraphs[0]; f.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r=f.add_run('PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT'); r.font.size=Pt(8); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)

def add_cover_to_redline(doc):
    # insert at front in reverse order
    first = doc.paragraphs[0]
    items=[]
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r=p.add_run('SELLER’S REDLINE / ANNOTATED MARKUP'); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(18); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r=p.add_run('Transition Services Agreement — Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. / Trident Manufacturing Group, Inc.'); r.font.size=Pt(11); r.bold=True
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r=p.add_run('Draft dated April 28, 2025 | Seller-side markup | Prepared for Whitfield & Crane LLP'); r.font.size=Pt(9); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(8); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(4)
    r=p.add_run('Redline legend: '); r.bold=True
    r=p.add_run('red strikethrough = deletion; '); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); r.strike=True
    r=p.add_run('blue underline = seller addition; '); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE); r.underline=True
    p.add_run('yellow callouts = annotated seller comments (basis, risk, and negotiation position).')
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(8)
    r=p.add_run('Review note: '); r.bold=True
    p.add_run('This markup is keyed to the executed APA excerpts supplied for review, particularly APA §7.12 and Exhibit H. Where the APA controls, the seller comment identifies the change as a must-change. The full executed APA controls in the event of any discrepancy.')
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)

# ---------- redline ----------

Service Provider shall ensure that the individuals identified on Schedule H attached hereto (the \"Key Personnel\") are assigned to perform the Services during the Term at the FTE allocation levels set forth on Schedule H. Service Provider shall not reassign, transfer, terminate (other than for cause as determined by Service Provider in its reasonable judgment), or otherwise remove any Key Personnel from the performance of the Services without the prior written consent of Service Recipient, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. In the event that any Key Personnel individual voluntarily resigns, becomes permanently disabled, or is terminated for cause, Service Provider shall promptly notify Service Recipient and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to replace such individual with a person of substantially similar qualifications, experience, and skill within thirty (30) days, subject to Service Recipient’s prior written approval of the replacement (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed). Service Provider acknowledges that the Key Personnel possess specialized knowledge of the Business and that their continued involvement is material to the successful transition of the Business to Service Recipient.",
 "Section 4.3 Staffing and Personnel. Service Provider shall retain sole discretion over the selection, assignment, reassignment, promotion, transfer, replacement, and termination of personnel providing the Services, including any personnel listed on Schedule H. Service Provider shall maintain reasonably qualified personnel sufficient to meet the applicable Service Standard. Service Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Service Recipient at least fifteen (15) Business Days’ advance written notice before reassigning or replacing any mutually agreed transition contact and shall assign a reasonably qualified replacement, but no Service Recipient consent shall be required and no individual shall be contractually dedicated or locked to the Services. Any FTE counts are estimates and may be adjusted in Service Provider’s reasonable discretion consistent with the Service Standard.") ,
('Section 5.2 Automatic Renewal.',
 "Section 5.2 Automatic Renewal. Upon expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive six (6)-month periods (each, a \"Renewal Term\"), unless Service Provider delivers written notice of non-renewal to Service Recipient at least one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the expiration of the then-current Initial Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. The Agreement may be renewed for up to two (2) successive Renewal Terms pursuant to this Section 5.2. During any Renewal Term, all terms and conditions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, including the Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule, subject to any adjustments expressly provided for herein. For the avoidance of doubt, the burden of providing notice of non-renewal rests solely with Service Provider; failure by Service Provider to deliver timely notice of non-renewal shall result in automatic renewal for the next succeeding Renewal Term (subject to the two (2) Renewal Term maximum).",
 "Section 5.2 No Automatic Renewal; Mutual Extension. This Agreement shall expire at the end of the Initial Term, and no automatic renewal or extension shall occur. The Parties may extend an individual Service only by a written amendment signed by both Parties, for a period not exceeding six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term, and only if the applicable extension pricing and scope are expressly agreed in that amendment. Any extension shall be an accommodation and shall not be effective by silence, inaction, or unilateral notice.") ,
('Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services.',
 "Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services. Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than one hundred twenty (120) days’ prior written notice to the other Party, provided that such notice specifies in reasonable detail the Service to be terminated and the effective date of termination. Termination of an individual Service shall not affect the continuance of any other Service being provided under this Agreement. Upon termination of an individual Service, the corresponding Fees for such Service shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of such termination.",
 "Section 5.3 Termination of Individual Services. Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon ninety (90) days’ prior written notice to the other Party, specifying the Service to be terminated and the effective date. Termination shall not affect any other Service. Buyer shall pay all Fees accrued through the effective date and reimburse Service Provider for non-cancelable costs or commitments incurred before receipt of the notice in reasonable reliance on continuation of the Service, subject to Service Provider’s commercially reasonable mitigation efforts.") ,
('Section 5.5 Effect of Termination.',
 "Section 5.5 Effect of Termination. Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part):",
 "Section 5.5 Effect of Termination. Upon termination or expiration of any Service or of this Agreement (in whole or in part), Service Provider’s obligation to provide the affected Services shall cease on the effective date, subject to any agreed Termination Assistance under new Section 5.7. Service Recipient shall pay all accrued but unpaid Fees, approved expenses, and non-cancelable costs within thirty (30) days. Each Party shall return or destroy the other Party’s Confidential Information, subject to legal and bona fide archival retention requirements, and all other rights and obligations shall cease except as expressly stated to survive.") ,
('Section 6.3 Payment.',
 "Section 6.3 Payment. Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within a commercially reasonable time following receipt thereof. All payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Service Provider in writing from time to time.",
 "Section 6.3 Payment. Service Recipient shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after the date of invoice. Any undisputed portion shall be paid when due notwithstanding a dispute concerning another portion. Late amounts shall accrue interest at the lesser of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law. Payments shall be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Service Provider.") ,
('Section 6.4 Fee Escalation.',
 "Section 6.4 Fee Escalation. The Fees set forth on the Fee Schedule are fixed for the duration of the Term and shall not be subject to escalation or adjustment, except as expressly provided in this Agreement.",
 "Section 6.4 Fee Escalation and Cost Adjustment. Subject to the APA, the Fees shall be adjusted on each anniversary of the Closing Date by the greater of (a) three percent (3%) or (b) the percentage increase in CPI-U for the trailing twelve (12) months. In addition, Service Provider may propose an adjustment for an Escalation Event, including a material increase in labor, benefit, system, vendor, regulatory, or other Fully-Loaded Costs or a material increase in volume or scope requested by Service Recipient. Any adjustment shall be calculated under the APA’s Fully-Loaded Cost definition, shall not increase the applicable markup above ten percent (10%), and shall be implemented through a written change order or amendment where required by the APA.") ,
('Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials',
 "Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — License Grant. Service Provider hereby grants to Service Recipient a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, and create derivative works of any Service Provider Materials (including any tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, or know-how) developed or utilized by Service Provider in connection with the performance of the Services under this Agreement. This license shall include the right to sublicense to Service Recipient’s Affiliates, successors, and assigns, and shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason. For the avoidance of doubt, the foregoing license extends to all Service Provider Materials that are used, in whole or in part, in the delivery of any of the Services, regardless of whether such Service Provider Materials were created specifically for the Services or existed prior to the Effective Date and were adapted or applied in the course of service delivery. Nothing in this Section 7.1 shall be construed to transfer ownership of any Service Provider Materials to Service Recipient; Service Provider retains all right, title, and interest in and to the Service Provider Materials, subject to the license granted herein.",
 "Section 7.1 Service Provider Materials — Ownership; No License. All Service Provider Materials, including tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, systems, know-how, and processes existing before or developed or used in connection with the Services, are and shall remain the sole and exclusive property of Service Provider or its licensors. No license, sublicense, right, or interest in any Service Provider Materials is granted to Service Recipient, except the limited, revocable right during the Term to access Service Provider systems solely to receive the Services in accordance with this Agreement. Service Recipient shall not copy, modify, reverse engineer, extract, create derivative works of, or use Service Provider Materials outside the Services. All access rights cease immediately upon expiration or termination, and any post-Term license must be documented in a separate written agreement with appropriate restrictions and compensation.") ,
('Section 8.4 Data Privacy.',
 "Section 8.4 Data Privacy. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws of the United States in connection with its performance under this Agreement, including with respect to the collection, use, processing, storage, transfer, and disposal of any personally identifiable information of employees, customers, or other individuals. Each Party shall implement and maintain appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect personal data against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.",
 "Section 8.4 Data Privacy; Mexican Data. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data privacy and data protection laws in connection with this Agreement, including U.S. laws and Mexico’s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties and its Regulations (LFPDPPP). For personal data of Monterrey Facility employees, Service Recipient is the data controller and Service Provider is the processor/service provider acting only on Service Recipient’s documented instructions and only to perform the Services. Service Recipient shall be responsible for providing compliant privacy notices (avisos de privacidad), establishing the lawful basis for processing, and obtaining any employee notices, consents, or other authorizations required for processing and cross-border transfer. The Parties shall document appropriate cross-border transfer mechanisms, limit access to personnel with a need to know, implement appropriate technical and organizational safeguards, assist with data-subject requests as reasonably required, and notify the other Party without undue delay of any actual or suspected unauthorized access, use, disclosure, loss, or security incident. Service Provider shall return or securely delete Service Recipient personal data at termination, subject to Applicable Law and bona fide archival retention requirements. Nothing in this Section creates an employment, agency, or co-employment relationship.") ,
('Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification.',
 "Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification. Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"Service Provider Indemnitee\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Provider Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:",
 "Section 9.1 Service Recipient Indemnification. Subject to Section 10.1, Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from third-party claims, losses, and reasonable documented defense costs arising out of Service Recipient’s operation of the Business after Closing, its use of or reliance on the Services, or its breach of this Agreement, except to the extent caused by Service Provider’s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct. This indemnity is limited to third-party claims and does not expand Service Recipient’s liability beyond the express remedies and limitations in this Agreement.") ,
('Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification.',
 "Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification. Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (each, a \"Service Recipient Indemnitee\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or suffered by any Service Recipient Indemnitee arising out of or relating to:",
 "Section 9.2 Service Provider Indemnification. Subject to Section 10.1, Service Provider shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Recipient and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents solely from third-party claims and reasonable documented defense costs to the extent directly caused by Service Provider’s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct in performing the Services. Service Provider shall not indemnify for ordinary negligence, any breach of this Agreement as such, any regulatory obligation of Service Recipient, or any loss arising from Service Recipient’s operation or use of the Services, except to the extent expressly provided above.") ,
('Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap.',
 "Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Service Provider’s aggregate liability arising out of or related to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or any other legal or equitable theory, shall not exceed an amount equal to two hundred percent (200%) of the total Service Charges actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider under this Agreement as of the date of the applicable claim (the \"Liability Cap\"). For the avoidance of doubt, the Liability Cap shall apply to all claims in the aggregate and not on a per-claim basis. This Section 10.1 shall not limit Service Provider’s liability for fraud, willful misconduct, or breaches of Article 8 (Confidentiality).",
 "Section 10.1 Aggregate Liability Cap. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the aggregate liability of Service Provider and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents to Service Recipient under or in connection with this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total Fees actually paid by Service Recipient to Service Provider during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing (the \"TSA Liability Cap\"). During the first twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, the TSA Liability Cap shall equal the total Fees actually paid from the Closing Date through the date of written assertion. Thereafter, it shall be calculated on a rolling twelve-month basis. This cap shall apply in the aggregate, not per claim, and shall be exclusive of any other cap or deductible. The cap shall not apply only to the exclusions required by APA §7.12(d): fraud or willful misconduct, breach of Article 8, and indemnification obligations for third-party claims to the extent resulting from the indemnifying party’s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.") ,
('Section 10.2 Consequential Damages.',
 "Section 10.2 Consequential Damages. SERVICE PROVIDER HEREBY WAIVES, AND SHALL NOT ASSERT, ANY AND ALL CLAIMS AGAINST SERVICE RECIPIENT FOR CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, DIMINUTION OF VALUE, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SUCH DAMAGES ARE BASED ON CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, AND REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SERVICE PROVIDER HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING WAIVER SHALL APPLY EVEN IN THE EVENT OF THE FAILURE OF ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF ANY REMEDY.",
 "Section 10.2 Mutual Waiver of Consequential Damages. NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING loss of revenue, loss of profits, loss of business opportunity, cost of replacement services, diminution in value, or loss of goodwill, regardless of the theory of liability or whether the party has been advised of the possibility of such damages. This waiver applies even if any remedy fails of its essential purpose and shall not limit liability for third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under this Agreement. The Parties intend this Section to be mutual and to conform to APA §7.12(d).") ,
('Section 11.2 Service Provider Representations.',
 "Section 11.2 Service Provider Representations. Service Provider further represents and warrants to Service Recipient as of the Effective Date that:",
 "Section 11.2 Limited Service Provider Representation. Service Provider represents only that, as of the Effective Date, it has the authority to enter into this Agreement and expects to have reasonably qualified personnel and existing systems available to provide the Services in a manner substantially consistent with the Service Standard. Service Provider does not warrant that the Services will be uninterrupted, error-free, compliant with every Applicable Law in every jurisdiction, or sufficient to achieve any particular result. Service Recipient remains responsible for its own operations, decisions, filings, and legal and regulatory compliance after Closing.") ,
('Section 12.1 Force Majeure.',
 "Section 12.1 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performing its obligations under this Agreement to the extent such failure or delay results from a Force Majeure Event. The affected Party shall: (a) promptly notify the other Party in writing of the Force Majeure Event, describing in reasonable detail the nature of the event and the expected duration thereof; (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance of its obligations as soon as practicable; and (c) keep the other Party reasonably informed of the status of such Force Majeure Event and its efforts to resume performance. The non-affected Party shall cooperate in good faith with the affected Party’s mitigation efforts. A Force Majeure Event shall not excuse the affected Party’s obligation to make any payment that was due and owing prior to the occurrence of such Force Majeure Event.",
 "Section 12.1 Force Majeure. Neither Party shall be liable for a failure or delay caused by a Force Majeure Event beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, pandemics, war, terrorism, government action, sanctions, embargoes, strikes, power failures, internet or telecommunications outages, or cyberattacks. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other Party, use commercially reasonable mitigation efforts, and keep the other Party reasonably informed. Obligations are suspended, not terminated, during the event, and payments due before the event remain payable. If the event continues for ninety (90) consecutive days, either Party may terminate the affected Service without penalty on written notice.") ,
('Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance.',
 "Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance. Service Recipient shall maintain, at its own expense, during the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months following the expiration or termination of this Agreement, commercial general liability insurance with a per-occurrence limit of not less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) and an annual aggregate limit of not less than Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000), issued by an insurer rated not less than \"A-\" (Excellent) by A.M. Best Company. Such insurance shall provide coverage for bodily injury, property damage, personal injury, and advertising injury arising out of or relating to Service Recipient’s operations and performance under this Agreement.",
 "Section 13.1 Service Recipient Insurance. Service Recipient shall maintain, at its own expense, during the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence and $5,000,000 aggregate; (b) umbrella or excess liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000; and (c) workers’ compensation insurance at statutory limits. Polaris shall be named as an additional insured under the CGL and umbrella/excess policies, and each policy shall include a waiver of subrogation in favor of Polaris. Certificates and endorsements shall be delivered within ten (10) Business Days after Closing and annually thereafter. Coverage shall be maintained with insurers rated at least A- by A.M. Best.") ,
('Section 14.1 Audit Rights.',
 "Section 14.1 Audit Rights. Service Recipient shall have the right, at Service Provider’s expense, to audit the books, records, systems, and supporting documentation of Service Provider relating to the Service Charges and the performance of the Services up to two (2) times per calendar year. Service Recipient shall provide Service Provider with at least ten (10) Business Days’ prior written notice of any such audit, specifying the scope and expected duration of the audit. Audits shall be conducted during normal business hours at Service Provider’s principal offices or such other location where the applicable records are maintained and shall not unreasonably interfere with Service Provider’s business operations. Service Recipient may conduct such audits using its internal audit personnel or an independent third-party auditor selected by Service Recipient (at Service Provider’s expense); provided that any third-party auditor shall be bound by confidentiality obligations reasonably satisfactory to Service Provider. Service Provider shall cooperate fully with any audit conducted under this Section 14.1 and shall provide reasonable access to its personnel, books, records, systems, and facilities.",
 "Section 14.1 Audit Rights. Service Recipient may, at its sole expense, audit Service Provider’s fee-related books and records once in any twelve (12)-month period, on at least thirty (30) Business Days’ prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Service Provider’s operations. The audit shall be limited to records reasonably necessary to verify Fees and shall exclude proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, security controls, trade secrets, and unrelated personnel records. Any auditor shall be independent, bound by confidentiality, and have no conflict of interest. Service Recipient shall keep audit results confidential and shall not disclose them except to its professional advisers bound by confidentiality or as required by law.") ,
('Section 15.1 Governing Law.',
 "Section 15.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Ohio, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.",
 "Section 15.1 Governing Law. This Agreement and all claims arising out of or relating to it shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.") ,
('Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution.',
 "Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution. Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, shall be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Cuyahoga County, Ohio. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts for the purpose of any such dispute, controversy, or claim and irrevocably waives, and agrees not to assert by way of motion, defense, or otherwise, any objection to such jurisdiction or venue, including any objection based on the doctrine of inconvenient forum or any objection to the laying of venue in Cuyahoga County, Ohio. EACH PARTY HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ALL RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION, PROCEEDING, OR COUNTERCLAIM ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT.",
 "Section 15.2 Dispute Resolution. Any dispute shall first be escalated to the Parties’ designated CFO or General Counsel representatives, who shall have fifteen (15) Business Days to resolve it. The Parties may then submit the dispute to non-binding mediation. If unresolved, the dispute shall be finally resolved by confidential, binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, before one arbitrator with relevant industry experience. Judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. Either Party may seek provisional injunctive relief to protect Confidential Information or intellectual property pending arbitration.") ,
('Section 15.3 Notices.',
 "Section 15.3 Notices. All notices, requests, demands, consents, waivers, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given: (a) when delivered by hand or by a nationally recognized overnight courier service (receipt requested); (b) on the date sent by email (with confirmation of transmission), provided that a copy is also sent by overnight courier service on the same day; or (c) on the third (3rd) Business Day after deposit in the U.S. mail, by certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid. All notices shall be addressed as follows:",
 "Section 15.3 Notices. Notices shall be in writing and effective upon receipt if delivered by hand or when received by nationally recognized overnight courier; by email with confirmation of transmission during normal business hours of the recipient (or the next Business Day if sent after hours); or on the third (3rd) Business Day after certified or registered mail, return receipt requested. Notices shall be sent to the addresses and contacts below, as updated by notice. The email-and-courier method in the draft is deleted to conform to APA §12.1.") ,
]

def add_issue_table(title, issues):
    m.add_heading(title, level=1)
    cols=['Issue / draft location','Basis / risk','Recommended seller position']
    t=m.add_table(rows=1, cols=3); t.style='Table Grid'; t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for c,txt in zip(t.rows[0].cells,cols): set_cell_text(c,txt,bold=True,color='FFFFFF',size=8); set_cell_shading(c,DARK)
    for issue,basis,risk,pos in issues:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        set_cell_text(cells[0],issue,bold=True,size=8)
        set_cell_text(cells[1],basis+'\n\nRisk: '+risk,size=8)
        set_cell_text(cells[2],pos,size=8)
    return t

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path('/home/agarwaldi/dsh-bench-harness/runs/hv-mixed200-lunahigh-flip-r7-20261118T030322Z/tasks/corporate-ma__draft-markup-of-transition-services-agreement-tsa/workspace')
OUT = ROOT/'output'
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
SRC = ROOT/'documents/trident-draft-tsa.docx'

RED = 'C00000'; BLUE = '0000FF'; GOLD = 'FFF2CC'; LIGHTBLUE = 'EAF3FF'; GRAY='666666'; DARK='1F4E79'

# ---------- helpers ----------
def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    borders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if borders is None:
        borders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(borders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge); element = borders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag); borders.append(element)
            for k,v in kwargs[edge].items(): element.set(qn('w:'+k), str(v))

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true'); trPr.append(tblHeader)

def set_cell_text(cell, text, bold=False, color=None, size=9):
    cell.text = ''
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    r = p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.font.size=Pt(size)

def add_field_run(p, label, value, color='000000'):
    r=p.add_run(label); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    r=p.add_run(value); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)

def add_comment_after(doc, anchor, cid, priority, basis, risk, position):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.style = doc.styles['Comment Callout']
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.35)
    p.paragraph_format.right_indent = Inches(0.15)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(2); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
    run=p.add_run(f'SELLER COMMENT {cid} — {priority.upper()}\n'); run.bold=True; run.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
    for lab,val in [('Basis: ',basis),('Risk to Polaris: ',risk),('Position: ',position)]:
        rr=p.add_run(lab); rr.bold=True; rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
        rr=p.add_run(val+'\n' if lab!='Position: ' else val); rr.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string('333333')
    # light shading and left border
    pPr=p._p.get_or_add_pPr(); shd=OxmlElement('w:shd'); shd.set(qn('w:fill'), GOLD); pPr.append(shd)
    pBdr=OxmlElement('w:pBdr'); left=OxmlElement('w:left'); left.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); left.set(qn('w:sz'),'18'); left.set(qn('w:space'),'6'); left.set(qn('w:color'), DARK); pBdr.append(left); pPr.append(pBdr)
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    return p

def insert_para_after(doc, anchor, text, style='Normal', color=None, bold=False, underline=False, strike=False):
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.style=style
    r=p.add_run(text); r.bold=bold; r.font.size=Pt(9.5)
    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    r.underline=underline; r.strike=strike
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    return p

def redline_para(p, old, new, heading=False):
    p.clear()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    r=p.add_run(old); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); r.font.strike=True
    r=p.add_run('\n'); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    r=p.add_run(new); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE); r.font.underline=True

def find_para(doc, startswith):
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if p.text.strip().startswith(startswith): return p
    raise KeyError(startswith)

def add_comment_for_prefix(doc, prefix, cid, priority, basis, risk, position):
    p=find_para(doc,prefix); add_comment_after(doc,p,cid,priority,basis,risk,position); return p

def style_doc(doc):
    styles=doc.styles
    normal=styles['Normal']; normal.font.name='Arial'; normal.font.size=Pt(9.5)
    for name in ['Heading 1','Heading 2','Heading 3']:
        st=styles[name]; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
    if 'Comment Callout' not in styles:
        st=styles.add_style('Comment Callout', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
        st.base_style=styles['Normal']; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    # footer

    r=p.add_run('Transition Services Agreement — Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. / Trident Manufacturing Group, Inc.'); r.font.size=Pt(11); r.bold=True
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    r=p.add_run('Draft dated April 28, 2025 | Seller-side markup | Prepared for Whitfield & Crane LLP'); r.font.size=Pt(9); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(8); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(4)
    r=p.add_run('Redline legend: '); r.bold=True
    r=p.add_run('red strikethrough = deletion; '); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); r.strike=True
    r=p.add_run('blue underline = seller addition; '); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE); r.underline=True
    p.add_run('yellow callouts = annotated seller comments (basis, risk, and negotiation position).')
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(8)
    r=p.add_run('Review note: '); r.bold=True
    p.add_run('This markup is keyed to the executed APA excerpts supplied for review, particularly APA §7.12 and Exhibit H. Where the APA controls, the seller comment identifies the change as a must-change. The full executed APA controls in the event of any discrepancy.')
    first._p.addprevious(p._p)

# ---------- redline ----------

    if color: r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    r.underline=underline; r.strike=strike
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    return p

def redline_para(p, old, new, heading=False):
    p.clear()
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(6)
    r=p.add_run(old); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(RED); r.font.strike=True
    r=p.add_run('\n'); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)
    r=p.add_run(new); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(BLUE); r.font.underline=True

def find_para(doc, startswith):
    for p in doc.paragraphs:
        if p.text.strip().startswith(startswith): return p
    raise KeyError(startswith)

def add_comment_for_prefix(doc, prefix, cid, priority, basis, risk, position):
    p=find_para(doc,prefix); add_comment_after(doc,p,cid,priority,basis,risk,position); return p

def style_doc(doc):
    styles=doc.styles
    normal=styles['Normal']; normal.font.name='Arial'; normal.font.size=Pt(9.5)
    for name in ['Heading 1','Heading 2','Heading 3']:
        st=styles[name]; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(DARK)
    if 'Comment Callout' not in styles:
        st=styles.add_style('Comment Callout', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH)
        st.base_style=styles['Normal']; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(8.5)
    # footer
    for sec in doc.sections:
        f=sec.footer.paragraphs[0]; f.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        r=f.add_run('PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT'); r.font.size=Pt(8); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(GRAY)

# helper memo tier table
def add_issue_table(title, issues):
    m.add_heading(title, level=1)
    cols=['Issue / draft location','Basis / risk','Recommended seller position']
    t=m.add_table(rows=1, cols=3); t.style='Table Grid'; t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for c,txt in zip(t.rows[0].cells,cols): set_cell_text(c,txt,bold=True,color='FFFFFF',size=8); set_cell_shading(c,DARK)
    for issue,basis,risk,pos in issues:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        set_cell_text(cells[0],issue,bold=True,size=8)
        set_cell_text(cells[1],basis+'\n\nRisk: '+risk,size=8)
        set_cell_text(cells[2],pos,size=8)
    return t
