('C2 — §5.2 Automatic Renewal','APA §7.12(a) hard-stops the Transition Period at 18 months, allows only a mutually signed extension up to six additional months, and bans automatic renewal.','Automatic renewal can extend services without Polaris’s affirmative consent and keep fees fixed.','Delete automatic renewal; any extension must be a mutual signed amendment, maximum six months, with separately agreed extension economics.'),
('C3 — §5.3 Service Termination','APA §7.12(c) sets both minimum and maximum notice at 90 days.','120 days exceeds the agreed maximum and delays redeployment; draft also omits non-cancelable-cost reimbursement.','Use 90 days and add reimbursement for non-cancelable commitments incurred before notice, subject to mitigation.'),
('C4 — §10.1 Liability Cap','APA §7.12(d): fees actually paid during rolling 12 months; limited exclusions.','Draft uses 200% of total fees. Exposure is ~$41.004M at draft fees versus ~$13.464M required; delta ~$27.540M.','Replace with APA-compliant initial-period and rolling-12-month cap, with only APA exclusions.'),
('C5 — §10.2 Consequential Damages','APA §7.12(d) requires a mutual waiver.','One-way waiver protects Trident but leaves Polaris exposed to business interruption, lost profits, replacement-service, and supply-chain claims.','Make the waiver mutual and preserve the APA third-party indemnification carve-out.'),
('C6 — Schedule B / Schedule G IT fee','APA §7.12(b) and Exhibit H: uniform 10% maximum; IT should be $374,000/month.','Draft uses 15% and $391,000/month, overcharging $17,000/month and $306,000 over 18 months if constant.','Correct IT markup to 10%, monthly fee to $374,000, and total to $1,122,000/month.'),
('C7 — §6.4 / Schedule G §5 Fee Adjustments','APA §7.12(b) requires actual Fully-Loaded Cost adjustments and a five-percent consent threshold.','Draft says fees are fixed and not adjustable, which can waive the APA mechanism and leave Polaris below cost.','Restore APA adjustment mechanics; retain markup cap and consent threshold; layer any escalation on top only if APA-compliant.'),
('C8 — §8.4 and new §12.3 Mexico provisions','APA §7.12(g) requires IMMEX and LFPDPPP terms.','Draft covers only U.S. privacy law and is silent on IMMEX certification, reporting, temporary imports, notices, consents, safeguards, and breach allocation.','Add buyer-primary IMMEX responsibility, limited paid transition assistance, LFPDPPP controller/processor terms, privacy notices/consents, transfer mechanisms, security, and breach notices. Confirm details with Mexico counsel.'),
]
add_issue_table('Priority 1 — Critical / Must-Change',critical)

significant=[
('S1 — §7.1 IP license','Playbook §6.1 is a firm no-license position.','Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free rights to tools, methodologies, software, know-how, modification, derivatives, and sublicensing create enterprise-wide IP leakage.','Delete license. Reserve all Polaris IP; allow only revocable system access during the Term to receive Services. Any post-Term need requires separate paid license.'),
('S2 — §4.3 / Schedule H personnel lock-up','Playbook §7.1 and APA Exhibit H treat FTEs as estimates adjustable by Seller.','Buyer consent over named individuals and allocations interferes with employee management and may create employment-law complications.','Polaris retains sole staffing discretion; provide notice and reasonably qualified replacements without consent.'),
('S3 — §§9.1–9.2 indemnities','Playbook §5.3 and APA §7.12(d) focus indemnity on third-party claims and gross negligence/fraud/willful misconduct.','Draft creates broad direct indemnity for any breach, legal violation, use, and reliance, undermining the cap.','Limit both indemnities to third-party claims; keep Trident’s use/operation risk with Trident; keep Polaris threshold at gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct; subject to cap as required.'),
('S4 — New §5.7 termination assistance','Playbook §3.4 requires a bounded, paid wind-down.','Silence invites indefinite post-termination support claims.','Add up to 60 days at cost-plus-15%, only on request and while invoices are current; scope limited to knowledge transfer, data migration, documentation, and replacement-provider cooperation.'),
('S5 — New §6.7 change orders','Playbook §4.4 requires signed bilateral change orders; APA allows >10% only for agreed Additional Services.','No procedure permits informal scope creep and unpriced volume/scope expansion.','Require signed change order, Polaris discretion, no performance before signature/advance payment, cost-plus-15% target.'),
('S6 — §6.3 payment','Playbook §4.3: Net 30, late interest, undisputed amounts paid.','“Commercially reasonable time” is vague and lacks late-payment economics.','Use Net 30, 1.5%/month (1.0% fallback), and express undisputed-payment obligation.'),
('S7 — §6.4 fee escalation','Playbook §4.2 targets greater of 3% or CPI-U plus Escalation Event.','Fixed pricing transfers inflation, benefit, vendor, regulatory, and volume risk to Polaris.','Add annual escalation and cost-event mechanics subject to APA limits.'),
('S8 — §§12.1–12.2 force majeure','Playbook §10 requires 90-day termination trigger and expressly covers cyber/internet/telecom.','No trigger leaves Polaris obligated indefinitely after prolonged disruption.','Add 90-day termination right for affected Services and expand event list.'),
('S9 — §13.1 buyer insurance','Playbook §8.1: $5M CGL + $5M umbrella, statutory WC, additional insured, waiver of subrogation, certificates.','Draft has only $2M CGL and no umbrella/additional-insured protection.','Move to $5M target; $3M CGL + umbrella is absolute fallback; add endorsements and certificate delivery.'),
('S10 — §14.1 audit rights','Playbook §9: once per 12 months, 30-Business-Day notice, buyer cost, fee records only.','Draft allows twice yearly, ten-day notice, seller-paid audits, systems/personnel access, and no confidentiality or threshold.','Narrow audit scope; buyer pays; 30-day notice; one audit per year; confidential results; 5% overcharge threshold for cost reimbursement.'),
('S11 — §§15.1–15.2 law/venue','Playbook §11: Pennsylvania law and AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh; litigation in buyer forum rejected.','Ohio law and Cuyahoga County litigation create home-court and public-dispute risk.','Use Pennsylvania law, executive escalation, optional mediation, and confidential AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh; Delaware is fallback if needed.'),
('S12 — Missing non-solicitation','Playbook §7.2 requires 12-month post-service protection for all service-providing employees.','Trident can hire Polaris’s shared-services personnel after gaining access to them through the TSA.','Add 12-month restriction with general-solicitation and no-cause termination exceptions; six months is absolute fallback.'),
('S13 — §11.2 service provider warranties','Playbook rejects outcome guarantees; historical performance is the benchmark.','Broad capability and all-laws warranties increase strict liability for a transitional accommodation.','Delete or narrow to authority and reasonable expectation of available resources; disclaim uninterrupted/error-free/result warranties.'),
('S14 — Schedule scope creep','Schedules A–F contain open-ended reports, Tier 3 IT, onboarding, supply-agreement guarantees, and transfer-pricing advisory language.','These provisions exceed or are less qualified than Exhibit H and can require new resources or third-party consents.','Conform to Exhibit H, historical practices, third-party-consent limitations, and change-order treatment for extras.'),
]
add_issue_table('Priority 2 — Significant / Major Playbook Deviations',significant)

minor=[
('M1 — §15.3 notices','APA §12.1 is receipt-based and addresses after-hours email.','Draft’s same-day email/courier formulation may create effectiveness disputes.','Conform mechanics to APA; preserve current addresses and contacts.'),
('M2 — §13.2 Polaris insurance','Draft requires $5M CGL and E&O for Polaris without tying the obligation to existing programs or the liability cap.','Could impose unnecessary dedicated coverage and cost on the service provider.','Clarify that Polaris may satisfy requirements through existing policies and has no obligation to procure dedicated insurance solely for TSA Services; consider deleting E&O requirement.'),
('M3 — §4.4 monthly reporting','Monthly FTE-hour reporting and “such other information” may expose internal cost allocation and create recurring administrative burden.','Reporting can become a backdoor audit or proprietary-methodology disclosure.','Limit reporting to service status, material issues, and migration milestones; fee support remains subject to the narrowed audit clause.'),

22:The first draft is materially buyer-favorable and should not be circulated as-is. The redline corrects seven direct APA conflicts, addresses the two board-level concerns (liability/IP), and adds the Mexico-specific provisions required by APA §7.12(g). The most urgent corrections are: (i) service standard, term/renewal, and individual-service notice; (ii) fee markup and fee-adjustment mechanics; (iii) the liability cap and unilateral damages waiver; and (iv) IMMEX/LFPDPPP allocation.
24:The liability-cap issue is the clearest quantified exposure. At the draft's current stated monthly fees, a 200%-of-total-fees cap could reach approximately \$41.004 million over an 18-month run, versus an APA-mandated rolling twelve-month cap of approximately \$13.464 million. That is approximately \$27.540 million of excess nominal exposure, or 3.05x the APA cap. Using the APA/Exhibit H fee table (which corrects the IT markup), the draft formulation would still be approximately \$40.392 million versus \$13.464 million.
